Hello Visionary!
 We empower our people to stay resilient and relevant in a constantly changing world. We’re looking for people who are always searching for creative ways to grow and learn. People who want to make a real impact, now and in the future. Does that sound like you? Then it seems like you’d make an outstanding addition to our vibrant team. Siemens Mobility is an independent run company of Siemens AG. Its core business includes rail vehicles, rail automation and electrification solutions, turnkey systems, intelligent road traffic technology and related services. In Mobility, we help our customers meet the need for hard-working mobility solutions. We’re making the lives of people who travel easier and more enjoyable while constantly developing new, intelligent mobility solutions!
 We are looking for Traction System Engineer
 You’ll make a difference by
 Understanding the Customer requirements and develop the Electrical system concept of the
 complete vehicle level and develop the sub system concepts.
 Collects external (customer, standards) and internal (rolling stock) requirements, allocates them
 to the technical teams.
 Defines the architecture and functionalities of the traction drive / auxiliary converter system/
 Energy storage (Battery), taking as input the external requirements as well as internal ones
 Derive the vehicle level performance requirements and discuss with the project teams and assist
 them to optimize the customer requirements.
 Ensures consistency and compatibility between all traction/ auxiliary system functions
 specifications by verifying every component specification and by participating in all design
 reviews
 Develop the traction convertor / Auxiliary convertor / Traction Motor / Traction
 Transformer/Battery working concepts and generate the Component specifications for the
 Vendors.
 Define the High Voltage components specifications & HV Architecture and work closely with
 vendors to develop a suitable component for a Locomotive/Metro/Commuter rail
 Develop design documentation and get design approval from customers.
 Developing system design (like Clause-by-Clause Comments, Performance simulations
 (MATLAB, PSIM, Python, Mathcad, Ansys, SABER or Similar tools etc) , Power scheme
 preparations, Component specification, Product Description / Specification, System block
 diagrams & Part list depending on customer requirement
 Preparation of System / Part - Verification & Validation - Specifications and validation in test lab & Train.
 Defining and performing Train verification strategy in close collaboration with all Engineering and
 Validation teams
 Conducting the Prototype tests on the sub systems and get the dispatch / design clearance from
 customer.
 Supports the traction / auxiliary system for implementation or update of the technical part of the
 risk mitigation plan along with Project technical manager
 Analyses technical issues and proposes solutions during the commissioning and the reliability
 growth phase
 Supports the traction / auxiliary by proposing QCD improvements.
 Coordination with Other engineering teams such as software, Brake, Circuit Engineering and
 Mechanical teams to develop electrical sub systems and integrate in the vehicle.
 Ability to define performance, braking strategy, slip/slide management, harmonic detection, on
 board energy storage functions, medium and low voltage supply, load management (AC/DC
 calculations)
 Knowledge of the sub-assemblies of a traction system (power module, control electronics, cooling
 system, etc.) and of their key features
 Responsible for: Technical open issues resolution, from investigation to modification implementation and problem closure
 Desired Skills
 You have successfully completed a master's degree in electrical engineering.
 You bring along relevant experience of 10-12 years in the field of traction technology for product
 design and system integration.
 Furthermore, you have knowledge of simulation tools / techniques for circuits of power
 electronics/IEC Standards/Traction Design Principles/ Components sizing/ Rolling Stock
 components
 You are familiar with analysis and review methodologies
 You are familiar with requirements, configuration and change management (DOORS or similar
 tools)
 You are capable of analysis and learning and always work Result, Team, and Quality Oriented.
 You are willing to travel as required for a project and collaborate with international colleagues.
 Good communication and presentation skills
 Knowledge of Power systems, earthing concepts, EMI-EMC protections, Validations as per IEC
 61287, IEC61377 etc.
 You will participate in the continuous development of competence and exchange ideas with
 teams on technological & Process topics
 Join us and be yourself!
 We value your unique identity and perspective and are fully committed to providing equitable opportunities and building a workplace that reflects the diversity of society. Come bring your authentic self and create a better tomorrow with us.
 Make your mark in our exciting world at Siemens.
 This role is based in Pune/Bangalore. You might be required to visit other locations within India and outside. In return, you'll get the chance to work with teams impacting - and the shape of things to come. We're Siemens. A collection of over 379,000 minds building the future, one day at a time in over 200 countries. We're dedicated to equality, and we encourage applications that reflect the diversity of the communities we work in. All employment decisions at Siemens are based on qualifications, merit and business need. Bring your curiosity and creativity and help us shape tomorrow.
Find out more about mobility at: https://new.siemens.com/global/en/products/mobility.html and about Siemens careers at: www.siemens.com/careers #SL

PCS Simulation & Control Engineer 
 Location: India | Experience: 3–8 years 
 SIFANG is looking for a PCS Simulation & Control Engineer to support the development of energy storage power conversion systems and solutions for international markets.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Develop simulation models and control strategies for energy storage Power Conversion Systems (PCS/DC-AC).
 Perform PCS and grid-connected system simulations using PSCAD to evaluate performance under different grid conditions.
 Develop and validate Fault Ride-Through (FRT) functions, including LVRT/HVRT and active/reactive power control during grid disturbances.
 Analyse and optimise three-level inverter topologies, modulation techniques and control algorithms.
 Collaborate with R&D and testing teams on model validation, troubleshooting and performance improvement.
 Provide technical support for international projects and work closely with engineering teams in China and overseas.
 Requirements 
 Bachelor’s degree or above in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Power Systems, Automation or a related discipline. A master’s degree is preferred.
 3–8 years of relevant experience in energy storage PCS, PV inverters or other grid-connected power converters.
 Hands-on experience with PSCAD , including independent model development, simulation and analysis.
 Strong understanding of DC-AC conversion and PCS control , including current/voltage loops, PLLs and active/reactive power control.
 Practical project experience in at least one of the following:
 FRT/LVRT: control development, simulation validation or testing.
 Three-level inverters: NPC or T-type topologies and PWM/SVPWM techniques.
 Good English communication skills and the ability to collaborate across international teams.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience with Grid-Forming control, VSG or droop control.
 Familiarity with MATLAB/Simulink and SIL/HIL validation.
 Experience with grid-code compliance, grid connection testing or commissioning.

Atmos Space Cargo 
 AOCS Engineer (m/f/d)
 Lichtenau, 77839, Germany 
 Permanent contract 
 On-site 
 Job description
 ATMOS Space Cargo GmbH is seeking an AOCS Engineer (m/f/d) to design, develop, integrate and validate Attitude and Orbit Control functions as well as Guidance, Navigation and Control algorithms for our reusable PHOENIX spacecraft. Working closely with Systems Engineering, Avionics and Flight Software, you will take ownership from algorithm design through testing and flight-data analysis. 
 Key responsibilities 
 You will develop and validate guidance, navigation and control algorithms for orbital flight, re-entry, descent and recovery. 
 You will translate mission objectives into AOCS / GNC architecture, interfaces, requirements and performance criteria. 
 You will build and maintain six-degree-of-freedom simulations and Monte Carlo campaigns to assess performance and robustness. 
 You will integrate AOCS / GNC functions with flight software and support software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop and system-level testing. 
 You will design operational procedures for the different phases of the mission, including LEOP and commissioning. 
 You will analyse test and flight data, resolve anomalies and drive technical decisions with Systems, Avionics, Propulsion and Aerodynamics teams. 
 Profile required
 Master's degree in aerospace engineering, control engineering, robotics, applied mathematics or a comparable technical field. 
 At least four years of professional experience in GNC, flight dynamics or autonomous-control development for spacecraft and launch vehicles. 
 Strong knowledge of flight mechanics, control theory, state estimation, numerical methods and uncertainty analysis. 
 Hands-on experience with MATLAB/Simulink, Python, and C++ or C including simulation, software integration and verification and validation. 
 Preferred qualifications 
 Experience with astrodynamics, space operations, mission modes and reentry vehicles. 
 Experience with embedded flight software, spacecraft sensors and actuators. 
 Knowledge of the European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) processes would be helpful. 
 Company description
 ATMOS was founded as a European company built on the values of freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law, and human rights. We are committed to protect these values by making our technology available to others who share the same values, strengthening infrastructure and innovation for prosperity on Earth. 
 Our team is multinational and diverse, with offices in Lichtenau and Strasbourg. We work in a collegial, hands-on culture where people support each other, take ownership, and keep learning every day. Motivation for the mission comes first — building spacecraft is not a nine-to-five pursuit. We align the mission, the team, and the individual in mutual dependence. This principle shapes our work environment where exceptional people, as committed as they are competent, can grow and contribute to a mission that matters.

BMS Algo design Engineer – Stationary Energy Storage (BESS)
 Location: Bengaluru, India
 Experience: 5–10 Years
 Function: BESS R&D and Engineering
 About The Role
 We are looking for an experienced BMS Algorithm Engineer to join our energy storage product development team . In this role, he should understand the BMS design, develop, validate, and deploy the estimation and control algorithms that run in our battery management system for C&I and utility-scale Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) . You will play a key role in ensuring system safety, reliability, scalability, and long-term performance across stationary storage applications such as grid support, renewable integration, and backup power.
 Key Responsibilities
 State Estimation (SOX)
 Develop and tune SoC, SoH, SoP, and SoE algorithms specific to LFP chemistry, handling the flat OCV-SoC curve, hysteresis, and long-term SoC drift. Methods include EKF/UKF, adaptive observers, OCV-reset strategies, and hybrid model plus data-driven approaches.
 Build and calibrate ECM and reduced-order electrochemical models from cell characterisation data (HPPC, OCV, EIS, capacity tests), and update parameters across temperature, SoC, and ageing.
 Design rack-level and system-level SoC/SoH aggregation across series-parallel strings, accounting for cell imbalance, rack-to-rack variation, and sensor error.
 Develop degradation and RUL models (calendar and cycle ageing) to support warranty terms, availability guarantees, and augmentation planning.
 Define accuracy targets for each estimate and validate them against lab and field data.
 Control and Protection
 Design cell balancing strategies (passive and active) for large strings, optimised for rest periods and low-C-rate daily cycling.
 Develop power derating and limit logic: charge/discharge current and power limits based on temperature, SoC, SoH, and cell voltage margins.
 Implement multi-level fault detection and diagnostics(module, rack, and container level):
 Over/under-voltage, over-current, and over-temperature
 Insulation and ground faults
 DC contactor and pre-charge faults
 Sensor and AFE faults
 Cell divergence
 Thermal runaway early warning (gas, temperature, and dV/dt signatures)
 Define BMS behaviour for safety escalation (alarm, derate, trip, shutdown) and its interface to fire detection and suppression systems.
 Define fault thresholds, debounce times, and recovery conditions, and document them in the safety and diagnostics specification.
 System Integration
 Define the BMS-to-PCS and BMS-to-EMS interfaces: limits, SoC/SoE reporting, alarms, heartbeat, and grid-event handling.
 Work with Modbus TCP/RTU, CAN/CAN-FD, IEC 61850, IEC 60870-5-104, DNP3, and OPC UA, based on project requirements.
 Support MIL/SIL/HIL testing, factory acceptance tests (FAT), site acceptance tests (SAT), and commissioning.
 Analyse fleet and SCADA data to detect drift, underperformance, and abnormal cell behaviour, and drive algorithm improvements through remote or OTA updates.
 Prepare algorithm design documents, test reports, and inputs for safety and compliance reviews.
 Required Skills & Experience
 Core Technical Skills
 5-10 years of experience in BMS, embedded systems, or energy storage product development.
 Strong fundamentals in battery electrochemistry, ECMs, and state estimation theory, with practical experience in Kalman filter variants, system identification, and parameter estimation.
 Hands-on experience with MATLAB/Simulink/Stateflow.
 Proficiency in C/C++ for embedded implementation, and Python for data analysis.
 Understanding of BMS architecture: AFE, MCU, hierarchical master-slave topology, contactors, and CAN communication.
 Experience with ML-based SoH/RUL prediction (LSTM, gradient boosting, etc.).
 Knowledge of P2D/electrochemical models (PyBaMM, COMSOL) or ageing models.
 Exposure to Model-Based Design and auto code generation (Embedded Coder).
 Experience with battery test equipment (Arbin, Bitrode, Maccor) and thermal chambers.
 Familiarity with AUTOSAR, CAN/CAN-FD/UDS, and tools like CANoe/CANalyzer, INCA, or dSPACE.
 System & Product Experience
 Experience working on stationary BESS products (commercial, industrial, or utility-scale preferred), ideally from design through deployment.
 Understanding of system-level interactions between BMS, PCS, EMS, and grid interfaces.
 Exposure to grid-relevant fault conditions (grid disturbances, PCS trips, communication loss) and long-duration operational requirements such as 10-15 year life and daily cycling.
 Awareness of how site conditions (ambient temperature, HVAC, fire safety systems) affect battery behaviour.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, Electronics, Embedded Systems, or a related discipline.
 Experience with high-voltage battery systems (up to 1000-1500 V DC) used in stationary storage.
 Knowledge of battery safety and compliance standards relevant to stationary storage, such as IEC 62619, UL 1973, UL 9540 / 9540A, IEC 62933, and NFPA 855.
 Familiarity with functional safety practices (FMEA/FMEDA, safety case documentation).
 Exposure to grid codes and ancillary service requirements.
 Experience with HIL platforms.
 Soft Skills
 Analytical, data-driven problem solving, comfortable working with messy field data
 Strong system-level thinking and problem-solving skills
 Ability to work independently in a product-driven environment
 Effective communication with cross-functional engineering teams, and with customers and EPCs when needed
 Detail-oriented mindset with a strong focus on reliability and safety
 Ownership from simulation through commissioning and long-term field performance

## Festanstellung \| Berlin \| Flexible Arbeitszeiten \| Vollzeit (40h)
## Gehalt: 56.000 € – 80.000 € pro Jahr, je nach Erfahrungslevel + weitere Benefits
Maßgeschneiderte Leistungselektronik statt Standard von der Stange.
Unser Mandant entwickelt komplexe Elektroniklösungen für unterschiedlichste Branchen. Genau dort, wo höchste Ansprüche auf technische Vielfalt treffen.
In seinem Auftrag suchen wir einen Entwickler Leistungselektronik (m/w/d), je nach Erfahrungslevel als Einstieg mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum oder als erfahrene Persönlichkeit mit Ownership für das große Ganze:
- Sie definieren Systemanforderungen und Schnittstellen und übernehmen im Team Verantwortung für eigene Arbeitspakete.
- Sie konzipieren Umrichtersysteme mit – von der Schaltungsidee über Layout und Validierung bis zur Serienfreigabe.
- Je nach Erfahrung wachsen Sie in die vollständige Systemverantwortung hinein bzw. bringen Sie von Tag eins mit.
Unabhängig von Ihrem Erfahrungsstand erwartet Sie technische Vielfalt, ein kollegiales Team auf Augenhöhe und die Chance, Produkte bis zur Serie mitzubringen. Bewerbungen von Berufseinsteigenden mit einschlägigem Studienschwerpunkt sind ausdrücklich willkommen.
## 
## Ihre Aufgaben
Konzeption, Auslegung & Design
- Sie definieren und stimmen die Anforderungen sowie elektrischen Schnittstellen für Umrichter und leistungsnahe Elektronik (Gate Drive Units, Schaltungen zur Strom- und Spannungserfassung, Stromversorgungen) ab und spezifizieren Systeme nach Kundenvorgaben.
- Sie übernehmen die elektrische und thermische Auslegung von Baugruppen inklusive der dazugehörigen Simulation in MATLAB/Simulink.
- Sie entwickeln analoge sowie digitale Schaltungen, erstellen die Leiterkarten-Layouts und begleiten den Prozess von der Datenübergabe über die Prüfung bis zur Serienfreigabe.
Prüfung, Validierung & Inbetriebnahme
- Sie planen und realisieren elektrische, thermische sowie Lebensdauertests im Labor und direkt am Fahrzeug und begleiten die Typtests der entwickelten Elektronik.
- Sie unterstützen die Inbetriebnahme und führen technische Schulungen direkt beim Kunden vor Ort durch.
Schnittstellen-, Lieferanten- & Lebenszyklusmanagement
- Sie arbeiten eng mit angrenzenden Fachbereichen zusammen – insbesondere bei der Abstimmung von Software-Schnittstellen mit der Softwareentwicklung sowie bei Vorgaben für die mechanische Konstruktion.
- Sie spezifizieren Zukaufteile (z. B. induktive Bauteile, Stromversorgungen) für den Einkauf und definieren Prüfvorgaben für Lieferanten.
- Sie verantworten die entwicklungsbegleitende Dokumentation (inklusive Zuarbeit für Schulungsunterlagen) und betreuen das Obsolescence-Management bei abgekündigten Bauteilen.
## 
## Ihr Profil
Qualifikation & Fachwissen
- Ein erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium der Elektrotechnik mit Schwerpunkt Leistungselektronik oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.
- Idealerweise erste oder mehrjährige Berufserfahrung in der Entwicklung leistungselektronischer Geräte und Komponenten.
- Fundierte Praxis in der Auslegung und Erprobung mittelfrequent taktender Schaltungen auf IGBT-Basis.
- Sicherer Umgang mit dem Design, Layout und Test analoger sowie digitaler Schaltungen – idealerweise mit gängigen EDA-/Layout-Tools (z. B. Altium Designer, EPLAN oder vergleichbare Software).
Arbeitsweise & Soft Skills
- Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift für die internationale Projekt- und Kundenarbeit.
- Eine selbstständige, analytische und zielorientierte Arbeitsweise gepaart mit Entscheidungsfreude und Kreativität.
- Ausgeprägte Team- und Kommunikationsfähigkeit, Flexibilität sowie eine hohe Einsatzbereitschaft.
## Das Angebot:
- Attraktives Vergütungspaket: 56.000 – 80.000 € pro Jahr, je nach Erfahrungslevel
- Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag in direkter Festanstellung beim Arbeitgeber
- Urlaubsanspruch von 30 Tagen im Kalenderjahr
- Flexible Arbeitszeiten ermöglichen Ihnen eine gesunde Balance zwischen Beruf und Privatleben.
- Weitere Benefits
## 
## Bereit für den nächsten Schritt als Entwicklungsingenieur Leistungselektronik (m/w/d) in Berlin?
PAN bietet Ihnen eine exklusive, persönliche Betreuung. Lassen Sie uns vertraulich miteinander sprechen. Wir beraten Sie offen, direkt und auf Augenhöhe und bieten eine persönliche Zusammenarbeit. Sie möchten mehr erfahren? Dann bewerben Sie sich jetzt!
## Gender-Hinweis
Aus Gründen der Lesbarkeit wird auf die gleichzeitige Verwendung aller Geschlechterformen verzichtet. Sämtliche Personenbezeichnungen gelten für alle Geschlechtsidentitäten. PAN lebt Vielfalt und Respekt.

About Pplwise
 pplwise is a recruiting consultancy for fast-growing technology companies across Europe. Through Recruiting as a Service and Executive Search, we fill key roles for our clients, from start-ups to publicly listed companies. We are filling this position for our client Filics.
 About our client: Filics
 Filics is reinventing intralogistics with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) that change how material moves. Its double-runner system makes Filics the first and only AMR that can drive through load carriers such as Euro pallets. This breaks with forklift logic and sets a new standard for efficiency. Filics is a small, hands-on team that solves hard problems with engineering excellence. Leadership goes to those who take initiative and consistently deliver. As Senior Electrical Engineer (m/f/d) at Filics, you will design the electronics at the core of the next generation of robots.
 About The Role
 This is an on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to engineering and assembly.
Filics doesn’t just use off-the-shelf components. It builds its own custom IP. The robots run on advanced boards that cover a wide range of electrical engineering. On one end is high power, such as battery and motor controllers. On the other end are high-speed interfaces like PCIe, USB and MIPI CSI. The real challenge is making all these subsystems work together as one system. Many of these problems have no textbook solution. Solving them takes solid experience, a deep understanding of the physics and a creative mind.
The EE team is small, and the robot is far from finished. You’ll own your boards end to end : requirements, system design, schematic, layout, design review, sourcing, manufacturing, testing and validation. You’ll keep owning them for as long as they’re in production. You’ll work closely with Embedded Software, Mechanical Engineering, Software and the Production team. As Filics moves from prototypes to series production, your designs need to work reliably at scale , not just in the lab.
 What You’ll Do
 Take full ownership of a complex PCB project and get it running in as few revisions as possible
 Design high-power and high-speed circuits and make sure they work together at system level
 Design for EMC, manufacturability and testability, and take boards through EMC testing and certification
 Bring new technical approaches to the team, for example a new converter architecture that enables higher charging power in a smaller package
 Introduce useful processes from your experience, such as simulation workflows that validate a layout before it goes to production
 Help with board bring-up and debugging together with Embedded Software, and support Production with clear documentation and training
 Take over ownership of existing boards so the team shares responsibility
 About You
 Several years designing electronics in an R&D environment at a smaller hardware company driven by innovation (e.g. robotics, e-mobility, aviation, autonomous vehicles, motion control)
 A proven record of taking PCBs within a larger system from requirements to a validated product
 Strong skills in schematic design and PCB layout (Altium, KiCad, OrCAD or similar)
 Hands-on debugging experience with an oscilloscope, logic analyzer, VNA or spectrum analyzer, plus soldering
 Experience with designs that went through EMC testing or CE certification
 An innovator’s mindset: you have built something new or significantly improved an existing concept
 Basic simulation know-how (e.g. LTspice, ANSYS, thermal/EM/tolerance analysis); deeper experience is a strong plus
 Basic experience with Linux and embedded software
 You work independently, take ownership and thrive without rigid structures
 What Filics Offers
 Real ownership of your designs, from first draft to series production
 Space to innovate and a wide range of technical challenges, from power electronics to high-speed design
 A small, high-caliber team with close collaboration across disciplines
 Fast growth: one year at Filics teaches you what usually takes many years at a large company
 An on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to Engineering and Assembly
 Sound like you? Apply with your CV.

 Qualifications and Experience

 Candidates with relevant industrial or academic research experience, particularly post-Ph.D. experience, will be given additional preference.
 Strong academic or professional background in Guidance, Navigation, and Control systems, spacecraft dynamics, control theory, and estimation algorithms.

 C/C++

 Git and Version Control
 Software Automation and Testing Tools

 GNC Sensors and Actuators

 Spacecraft AOCS/GNC Subsystems

 Why Bellatrix Aerospace?

 Job description
 ATMOS Space Cargo is seeking an Embedded Systems Engineer - Validation & Verification (m/f/d) to own verification and validation of the Phoenix capsule's embedded avionics and control systems, from test requirements through to a system proven to work in flight. You will design and operate our dSPACE-based hardware-in-the-loop test benches, and you will work across Avionics, Flight Software, GNC, and AIT to turn requirements into evidence that the system does what it should. 
 Key responsibilities 
 You will design, build, and operate dSPACE-based hardware-in-the-loop test benches, for example SCALEXIO, ControlDesk, and ConfigurationDesk, to simulate sensors, actuators, and environmental conditions. 
 You will derive test cases from system and software requirements and build automated test suites for embedded flight software and avionics components. 
 You will run verification and validation campaigns at unit, integration, system, and acceptance level, and produce the evidence of compliance against requirements. 
 You will analyze faults and debug at the interface between hardware, firmware, and flight software, and carry out root cause analysis of test anomalies. 
 You will maintain and extend the test infrastructure, including plant models, I/O configuration, and real-time simulation models. 
 You will work with the Avionics, Flight Software, GNC, and AIT teams, contribute to design reviews from a verification and validation perspective, and maintain the verification matrix and test documentation for qualification and acceptance. 
 Profile required
 Degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science or Embedded Systems, or a related field. 
 3+ years of experience in verification and validation of embedded systems, with hands-on work on hardware-in-the-loop test benches. 
 Hands-on experience with the dSPACE environment, such as ControlDesk, ConfigurationDesk, and SCALEXIO or MicroAutoBox. 
 Solid understanding of embedded hardware and firmware, including microcontrollers and communication buses such as Ethernet, CAN, RS-422/485, I2C, SPI, and SpaceWire. 
 Experience with test automation and scripting in Python, MATLAB, or Simulink. 
 A structured, self-driven way of working and enjoyment of troubleshooting at the intersection of hardware and software. 
 Very good written and spoken English; German is a plus. 
 Preferred qualifications 
 Experience in the space or aerospace industry, or with safety-critical and mission-critical systems. 
 Familiarity with relevant standards, mainly ECSS. 
 Experience with model-based development, Model-in-the-Loop and Software-in-the-Loop, alongside HIL. 
 Familiarity with requirements management tools such as Polarion. 
 Company description
 ATMOS was founded as a European company built on the values of freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law, and human rights. We are committed to protect these values by making our technology available to others who share the same values, strengthening infrastructure and innovation for prosperity on Earth. 
 Our team is multinational and diverse, with offices in Lichtenau and Strasbourg. We work in a collegial, hands-on culture where people support each other, take ownership, and keep learning every day. Motivation for the mission comes first — building spacecraft is not a nine-to-five pursuit. We align the mission, the team, and the individual in mutual dependence.  Job description
 ATMOS Space Cargo is seeking a Thermal Engineer (m/f/d) to support the thermal design, analysis and verification of our reentry and return vehicle technologies. You will work closely with multidisciplinary engineering teams to make sure our spacecraft hardware performs reliably across all mission phases, from launch and orbit operations to reentry and landing. 
 Your tasks 
 You will develop and maintain thermal models for spacecraft level thermal architecture, including active and passive thermal control design for avionic components and payloads. 
 You will perform thermal modeling across mission phases, including launch, orbit operations, de-orbit, re-entry, landing, and ground handling. 
 You will design, analyze, and integrate pumped fluid loops to manage heat collection and rejection for spacecraft survival in extreme orbital environments. 
 You will select and optimize COTS fans to maximize forced-air cooling efficiency while minimizing acoustic signatures and meeting outgassing standards for microgravity locker environments. 
 You will perform transient thermal analysis of spacecraft thrusters, including heat soak-back assessment, propulsion thermal modeling, and cross-functional coordination with propulsion, mechanical, and systems engineering teams. 
 You will define and manage flight hardware interfaces during integration, including pipes, fittings, valves, MLI, heaters, sensors, harness routing, thermal fillers, and related components. 
 You will design and plan thermal test campaigns, including Active Thermal Control System (ACTS), TVAC, thermal balance, and thermal cycling, at system and sub-system level. 
 You will work closely with mechanical, systems, avionics, and AIT teams to ensure technical alignment across subsystems and interfaces. 
 You will prepare and maintain thermal engineering documentation, including analysis reports, test procedures, verification plans, and review inputs. 
 Profile required
 Masters degree in Aerospace, Mechanical or Thermal Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field. 
 At least 3 years of professional experience in the aerospace industry, working on thermal control of spacecraft or satellites at spacecraft level. 
 Hands on experience building and correlating spacecraft level thermal models across mission phases. 
 Good knowledge of orbital mechanics, thermodynamics and fluid dynamics. 
 Solid understanding of conduction, convection, radiation and transient thermal behaviour. 
 Experience with thermal tools such as Simcenter 3D, TaiTherm, SimLab Thermal, Simulink, Matlab or Altair Flow Simulator. 
 Preferred qualifications 
 Experience with reentry vehicles, thermal protection systems or high temperature environments. 
 Experience supporting TVAC campaigns, thermal balance tests or hardware validation. 
 Knowledge of ECSS standards, Python or Matlab. 
 Company description
 ATMOS was founded as a European company built on the values of freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law, and human rights. We are committed to protect these values by making our technology available to others who share the same values, strengthening infrastructure and innovation for prosperity on Earth. 
 Our team is multinational and diverse, with offices in Lichtenau and Strasbourg. We work in a collegial, hands-on culture where people support each other, take ownership, and keep learning every day. Motivation for the mission comes first — building spacecraft is not a nine-to-five pursuit. We align the mission, the team, and the individual in mutual dependence. This principle shapes our work environment where exceptional people, as committed as they are competent, can grow and contribute to a mission that matters.

Über KnowWay
 KnowWay entwickelt KI-Agenten für kritische Infrastruktur: Energie, Telekommunikation und öffentlicher Sektor. Wir automatisieren Geschäftsprozesse mit autonomen Agenten, und zwar für Kunden, bei denen Compliance, Nachvollziehbarkeit und Datensouveränität Pflicht sind.
 Wir begleiten unsere Kunden über den gesamten Daten- und KI-Lebenszyklus. Wir sammeln und speichern die Daten, verarbeiten sie mit und für KI, sichern ihre Qualität und integrieren die Ergebnisse in produktive Systeme.
 Das Projekt
 Für einen führenden Telekommunikationskonzern in Deutschland setzen wir Daten- und KI-Projekte auf der Google Cloud um. Wir kennen die gesamte Prozess- und Systemlandschaft des Kunden, arbeiten darin und bauen mehrere Plattformen, auf denen die Fachbereiche ihre Anwendungsfälle betreiben. Mehrere Anwendungsfälle laufen parallel und stehen an unterschiedlichen Punkten zwischen Discovery und Live-Betrieb.
 Unser Delivery-Team deckt dabei ungewöhnlich viel ab: Business-Analyse und die Definition der eigentlichen Anforderungen, Solution Design, schnelle PoCs und die Produktivsetzung. Wo es passt, verwenden wir vorhandene Plattform-Capabilities wieder, und wo etwas fehlt, entwickeln wir es neu.
 Der Stack läuft bereits produktiv. Dazu gehören LLM-Extraktionspipelines über einen gemanagten AI-Service mit vorgeschaltetem Compliance-Proxy, agentische Systeme mit Vector Search, Batch-Verarbeitung und Orchestrierung, ein zentrales Data Warehouse und containerisierte Services. Die Infrastruktur ist komplett als Code beschrieben und läuft in einer streng abgeschotteten Umgebung mit mehreren Freigabestufen. Auf der Roadmap stehen unter anderem der Umbau des Query-Layers, die Anbindung von On-Premise-Systemen an Cloud-Worker und die Integration weiterer Quellsysteme.
 Die Rolle
 Du arbeitest mit uns dort, wo Datenpipelines, KI-Modelle und Cloud-Infrastruktur zusammenkommen. Gemeinsam mit dem Team sorgst Du dafür, dass das Ergebnis im Produktivbetrieb zuverlässig läuft, und übernimmst dabei nach und nach mehr Verantwortung. Jeder Schritt soll nachvollziehbar, überwacht und wartbar bleiben, auch wenn sich Datenmengen, Dokumentqualität oder Anforderungen ändern.
 Zwei Wege in diese Rolle
 Der Stack reicht von der Infrastruktur über Datenpipelines bis zu LLM- und Agentensystemen. Niemand bringt das alles auf Expertenniveau mit, deshalb beschreiben wir zwei Profile mit jeweils anderen Entwicklungsperspektiven. Wenn Du einen Schwerpunkt und die Bereitschaft hast, auch in die andere Richtung mitzudenken, dann ist die Rolle die Richtige für Dich.
 Profil A - Platform-Schwerpunkt : Deine Erfahrung liegt vor allem in GCP/Cloud-Infrastruktur, Infrastructure as Code und Deployment. Daten- und AI-Pipelines willst Du so weit verstehen, dass Du sie betreiben und debuggen kannst.
 Profil B - AI & Data-Schwerpunkt : Deine Erfahrung liegt vor allem in AI Engineering, LLM- und Datenpipelines und in Datenmodellierung. Die Infrastruktur darunter willst Du so weit verstehen, dass Du selbst deployen und Probleme bis in die Plattform verfolgen kannst.
 In der Rolle entwickelst Du Dich jeweils in die andere Richtung: Mit Profil A arbeitest Du Dich zunehmend in AI- und Datenthemen ein, mit Profil B in Infrastruktur und Plattform. Wir planen das bewusst ein, und Du übernimmst auf der anderen Seite nach und nach mehr Aufgaben.
 Die Rolle passt auch für Junior- und Mid-Level-Engineers. Wichtiger als viele Jahre Erfahrung ist uns, dass Du in einem der beiden Bereiche schon praktisch gearbeitet hast und Lust hast, Dich in den anderen einzuarbeiten. Die Anforderungen unten "für beide Profile“ + das A oder B-Profil sind das Minimum, mit dem Du einsteigen kannst. Wer mehr mitbringt, steigt entsprechend höher ein.

About the Role 
 As an Engineer, Enterprise Platforms, you will be a hands-on owner of the collaboration tools our employees use all day. You will administer, automate, and improve them, working alongside identity, endpoints, and the wider SaaS stack.
 This is a role for someone who sees a problem, figures out the fix, and ships it. Our team is small and the scope is broad. You will have real ownership early, a lot of autonomy, and few layers between you and the people you support. You will turn policies, runbooks, and employee needs into reliable configurations, scripts, and self-service experiences. We use AI tools where they make us faster or more accurate, and we expect good judgment about when to trust them.
 This role reflects Abnormal VOICE values. You move with velocity, design for long-term ownership and governance, use data with intellectual honesty, stay close to customer needs, and aim for excellence in reliability and simplicity.
 What You Will Do 
 Administer Google Workspace: users, groups, org units, shared drives, Drive sharing and DLP, Gmail routing and policies, Calendar and room resources, Meet, and audit and security investigation tooling.
 Administer Slack (Enterprise Grid): workspaces, channels, user groups, permissions, app approvals, Slack Connect, retention, export and eDiscovery, workflows, and audit logs.
 Build and maintain automation for joiner, mover, and leaver flows, access requests, deprovisioning, and common employee needs, using SCIM, APIs, webhooks, Apps Script, and scripting.
 Work with identity (Okta SSO, MFA, group-based access) so Google and Slack access follows least privilege and birthright rules.
 Support endpoints and other SaaS platforms as needed, including macOS device management and long-tail SaaS administration.
 Create self-service experiences, runbooks, and enablement content so employees can resolve common needs without escalation.
 Participate in Tier 2/3 incidents, perform root cause analysis, and feed what you learn back into automation, runbooks, and standards.
 Add logging, dashboards, and reporting so changes are monitored and audit questions can be answered quickly.
 Use AI tools where they help (documentation, troubleshooting, request triage, analysis), with human review and appropriate access controls.
 Partner with Security, GRC, Legal, People, Finance, and IT Service Delivery to deliver changes safely.
 Triage incoming requests and incidents by impact and urgency, route them to the right owner or queue, and resolve or escalate within agreed response targets.
 Turn vague or incomplete requests into clear requirements: ask clarifying questions, identify stakeholders and constraints, and confirm the desired outcome before building.
 Set clear expectations with employees and stakeholders about scope, timelines, and tradeoffs. Give status updates proactively, and flag risks or delays early.
 Governance and Compliance 
 Define and enforce standards for external sharing, Slack Connect, guest access, and third-party and OAuth app approval in Google Workspace and Slack.
 Run regular access and license reviews, using systems and audit logs to find unused, orphaned, or over-privileged access.
 Keep configuration baselines documented, changes tracked in ServiceNow, and evidence ready for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP audits.
 Review audit logs and investigate suspicious activity with Security.
 Document requirements, risks, and approvals for changes so they pass change review and can be audited later.
 Scripting and Automation 
 Automate first. If a task happens more than a couple of times, you script it, build a workflow, or turn it into self-service.
 Write scripts and tools (Python, Apps Script, and shell) against the Google Workspace, Slack, and Okta APIs.
 Build and maintain integrations and workflows in Workato, connecting identity, HR, collaboration, ticketing, and SaaS systems.
 Use Torii workflows to automate app discovery, onboarding and offboarding, and license reclamation.
 Build ServiceNow catalog items and flows so requests are routed, approved, and fulfilled with minimal manual touch.
 Keep scripts and configuration in version control, with logging, error handling, and clear documentation so others can run and maintain them.
 Our Tooling 
 Collaboration: Google Workspace, Slack (Enterprise Grid)
 Identity: Okta
 Automation and integration: Workato, Torii, Python, Apps Script
 Service management: ServiceNow
 Endpoints and other: Jamf, Zoom, and a long tail of SaaS applications
 You don't need experience with every tool. Strong experience with comparable platforms, and a record of learning new ones quickly, is what matters.
 How We Work 
 Automation-first: We remove repetitive work rather than absorbing it, and we measure success by manual touches eliminated.
 Customer-first: Employees are our customers. We respond with urgency, communicate clearly, and fix root causes so the same problem doesn't come back. We do what we say we'll do, or we tell people early when that changes.
 Fast-paced: Priorities shift quickly and requests arrive from every direction. We move fast, ship in small steps, and iterate.
 Time management and triage: You juggle incidents, requests, and project work. You sort what comes in by impact and urgency, handle what's urgent first, and protect focused time for project work and for the root-cause fixes that prevent tomorrow's tickets.
 What We're Looking For 
 You find the problem before someone assigns it, and you follow through to a documented, working fix.
 You are comfortable with ambiguity: unclear requirements, incomplete documentation, and shifting priorities don't stop you.
 You prioritize well when everything feels urgent. You set expectations early and honestly: you say no or "not yet" clearly and kindly, and you explain the reason.
 You learn new platforms quickly and teach what you learn.
 You ask the right questions up front: who needs this, what problem it solves, what 'done' looks like, and what could go wrong. You propose a recommended approach rather than waiting to be told.
 You communicate proactively: status updates, change notices, and honest post-incident write-ups.
 Must Haves 
 2+ years of experience in IT engineering, systems administration, or a similar role supporting business-critical technology.
 Hands-on administration of Google Workspace (Admin console, groups, Drive and sharing controls, Gmail, Calendar).
 Hands-on administration of Slack (workspace and channel management, user groups, app management, permissions). Enterprise Grid experience is a strong plus.
 Working knowledge of identity and access concepts: SSO, MFA, least privilege, directory and group management, and SCIM or standards-based provisioning.
 Ability to script and integrate systems using APIs, webhooks, Apps Script, Python, or similar tooling.
 Experience with incident and change management, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and documented follow-through.
 Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting technical processes and explaining complex systems to non-technical audiences.
 A track record of working independently and taking ownership without close direction.
 Experience writing scripts or building workflows that automate repetitive IT work, and a habit of automating before doing something manually a third time.
 A customer-first approach to supporting employees: responsive, clear, and focused on fixing root causes.
 Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and manage your time across incidents, requests, and project work, prioritizing by impact.
 Ability to set and manage expectations with stakeholders, including saying no or negotiating scope and timelines while keeping trust.
 Nice to Have 
 Experience at a startup or high-growth company, where you wore multiple hats, built processes from scratch, or scaled IT through rapid headcount growth. 
 Experience with acquisitions, tenant or domain migrations, or workspace consolidation. 
 Experience with data governance in collaboration tools: retention, legal hold, eDiscovery, DLP, and audit log analysis. 
 Google Workspace or Slack administration certifications, or involvement in their admin communities. 
 Experience with Okta, Jamf, Zoom, or other enterprise SaaS administration.
 Experience in remote-first, SaaS-first, or zero-trust environments.
 Familiarity with version control, configuration-as-code, or CI/CD for platform automation.
 Experience building self-service workflows, or using AI tools to improve support, troubleshooting, and documentation.
 Awareness of security and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP) as applied to collaboration and end-user platforms.
 Experience with Workato or a similar integration platform (Zapier, Tray.io, Boomi, or Okta Workflows).
 Experience with Torii or another SaaS management platform, such as Zluri or BetterCloud.
 Experience with ServiceNow (catalog items, flows, incident, request, and change) or a similar ITSM platform.
 Experience administering Microsoft 365 (Entra ID, Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint/OneDrive, or the M365 admin center), especially in a mixed Google and Microsoft environment.

About Bellatrix Aerospace
 Bellatrix Aerospace is a space technology company focused on developing innovative solutions for the global space industry. We work towards advancing space technologies through cutting-edge engineering, research, and development, contributing to the future of space exploration and satellite systems.
 Role Overview
 We are looking for a skilled and motivated Electromechanical Engineer to join our engineering team. The ideal candidate will be responsible for designing, developing, simulating, fabricating, and testing electromechanical actuation systems for space applications. The role involves working across mechanical design, electrical systems, mechanisms, and control systems, ensuring that all components and systems meet stringent engineering, performance, and quality requirements for space qualification.
 Key Responsibilities
 Design, develop, simulate, fabricate, and test electromechanical actuation systems for space applications.
 Collaborate with machinists and technicians to ensure that electromechanical systems meet design specifications.
 Translate electromechanical drawings into detailed design specifications using engineering principles, thermal and fluid sciences, mathematics, and statistical methods.
 Analyse engineering designs involving logic and digital circuitry, motor controls, instrumentation, and data acquisition systems for integration into automated and electromechanical systems.
 Direct and coordinate manufacturing support, technical documentation, and testing activities to ensure compliance with design specifications.
 Prepare, review, and verify technical drawings and electrical system specifications to ensure compliance with applicable standards.
 Identify and implement design modifications to address operational deficiencies and minimise fabrication challenges.
 Review technical documents and reports to ensure the accuracy of data, information, and engineering calculations.
 Evaluate, interpret, and implement commercial, military, and customer specifications related to materials, processes, and surface finishes.
 Conduct testing and qualification of electromechanical systems for space applications.
 Qualifications and Experience
 M.E./M.Tech./B.E./B.Tech. in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
 Minimum of 2 years of relevant industry experience.
 Experience with automated drafting, 3D modelling systems, and engineering analysis software.
 Hands-on experience in the design, engineering, and/or fabrication of mechanical and electromechanical components.
 Practical understanding of engineering design processes and system integration.
 Required Skills
 Strong knowledge of mechanics, actuation systems, mechanisms, and control systems.
 Excellent understanding of engineering fundamentals and design principles.
 Proficiency in 3D modelling, CAD tools, and engineering analysis software.
 Strong problem-solving and analytical abilities, with a creative approach to developing engineering solutions.
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to prepare clear and precise technical documentation.
 Ability to manage multiple projects and meet technical deadlines.
 Strong attention to detail and commitment to engineering quality.
 Why Bellatrix Aerospace?
 Be part of an innovative team working on advanced space technologies.
 Work on challenging engineering problems with real-world space applications.
 Gain hands-on experience in the design, development, and qualification of advanced electromechanical systems.
 Collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams and contribute to the development of next-generation space systems.
 Be part of a growing organisation shaping the future of the space industry.

Job Description:
 To support Airbus Defence and Space we are looking for a Cyber Security Hardware Architect (d/m/w).
Airbus DS is seeking a highly skilled Cyber Security Hardware Architect (d/m/w) to design, develop, and implement secure hardware solutions for our critical aerospace systems. This role is crucial in safeguarding our products against evolving cyber threats, ensuring the integrity and reliability of our cutting-edge technology. This role is also possible with reduced weekly working hours and an adapted scope of duties.
 Your Location
 Our site is just a stone's throw away from Munich, the beautiful capital of Bavaria. Do you enjoy sports and other outdoor activities? The Alps and Lake Starnberg can be reached within an hour and offer a wide variety of leisure activities.
 Our Benefits For You
 Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, e.g., company pension schemes, mobility offers (such as bicycle leasing), or employee discounts at cooperating companies in accordance with our respective valid guidelines.
 Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave according to the collective bargaining agreement (35h/week); work-life balance (flextime, mobile working, part-time, job sharing, sabbatical)
 Advancement Made Easy: Excellent training opportunities and international, group-wide development perspectives
 Well-being at the Workplace: Company doctor; comprehensive health offerings (sports courses, preventive care, and much more), canteen and cafeteria, partly on-site kindergarten
 Diversity Connects: Working in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, support, and diversity are lived
 Your Tasks And Responsibilities
 Define and develop robust cyber security architectures for hardware components and systems across various Airbus products.
 Conduct threat modeling, risk assessments, and vulnerability analysis of hardware designs and implementations.
 Specify and select secure hardware components, cryptographic modules, and security mechanisms.
 Collaborate with hardware design, software development, and system integration teams to embed security by design principles.
 Develop and implement security requirements, guidelines, and best practices for the hardware development lifecycle.
 Perform security reviews and audits of hardware designs, schematics, and layouts.
 Stay abreast of the latest hardware security vulnerabilities, attack vectors, and countermeasures.
 Contribute to the research and development of innovative hardware security solutions and technologies.
 Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers on hardware security topics.
 Desired Skills And Qualifications
 Master's degree or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Cyber Security, or a related field.
 Proven experience (5+ years) in hardware security architecture, design, and implementation.
 In-depth knowledge of hardware security principles, secure boot processes, trusted execution environments (TEE), and cryptographic hardware.
 Familiarity with industry standards and regulations related to hardware security (e.g., NIST, Common Criteria).
 Experience with hardware description languages (VHDL, Verilog) and FPGA/ASIC design.
 Strong understanding of embedded systems security and real-time operating systems.
 Knowledge of the Space and Aerospace domain, preferably having worked in the secure architecture of aerospace projects.
 Fluency in English is required; German or French is a plus.

Localisation
 Poste basé à Avignon  (84). 
 Vous souhaitez découvrir concrètement comment se développent les projets de stockage par batteries et contribuer à la transition énergétique ? Au sein de l’équipe Novar en France, vous serez accompagné·e par les équipes de développement et les supports techniques. Vous participerez, à votre niveau, à l’identification de sites et à la préparation des premières analyses et démarches d’autorisation pour des projets de stockage. Vous accompagnerez également dans leurs missions de développement de projets solaires les Développeurs Nouveaux Projets et les Chef.fe .s de projets.
 Vos missions
 ·         Identification de sites pour des projets de stockage par batteries. Pour cela, un travail d’analyse et de suivi des évolutions techniques et réglementaires devra être réalisé.
 ·         Analyses et prédimensionnement du projet de stockage sur la base des informations collectées (caractéristiques du réseau électrique à proximité ; règles d’urbanismes ; enjeux liés à l’occupation du sol, aux accès, au voisinage et aux zonages environnementaux).
 ·         Préparer des supports de synthèse (recherches documentaires, cartographie et tableaux de suivi) et apprendre à faire ressortir les principaux points à approfondir.
 ·         Accompagner les Chef.fe .s de projet en Développement et les Développeurs Nouveaux Projets dans leurs missions et se familiariser avec les démarches de sécurisation foncière, de développement de projets et de permitting sous leurs supervisions.
 Votre profil
 ·         Bac +5 type Master ou Ingénieur généraliste ou énergie .
 ·         Un intérêt marqué pour les énergies renouvelables, les systèmes électriques et la transition énergétique.
 ·         À l’aise avec la recherche, l’analyse et la synthèse d’informations, ainsi qu’avec la rédaction de documents clairs.
 ·         Rigueur, autonomie, curiosité et esprit d’équipe.
 ·         Bonne maîtrise des outils bureautiques ; la connaissance des outils SIG ou de la réglementation en urbanisme et en environnement constitue un plus.
 ·         Bon niveau de français ; la connaissance de l’anglais est appréciée dans notre environnement international.
 Ce que NOVAR vous offre
 Chez Novar, nous ne vous proposons pas seulement un emploi – nous vous invitons à rejoindre une véritable aventure. Vous travaillerez dans un environnement entrepreneurial et innovant, où l’énergie est au cœur de tout – au sens propre comme au sens figuré. Aux côtés de professionnels passionnés, vous contribuerez concrètement à la mise en œuvre de systèmes énergétiques durables.
 Et qu’est-ce que cela vous apporte? 
 💰 Une gratification de stage de 900 € par mois, dans le respect de la réglementation en vigueur.
 🚆 Remboursement de 50 % des frais de transport en commun.
📚 Des opportunités de développement et de croissance au sein de notre scale-up international.
 À propos de Novar – Nous façonnons l’avenir énergétique de l’Europe
 Chez Novar, nous croyons que l’avenir de l’énergie est vert – et nous le concrétisons. Depuis notre création en 2014 aux Pays-Bas, nous sommes devenus un acteur majeur du développement et de l’exploitation de grandes installations d’énergies renouvelables. Avec plus de 200 collaborateurs engagés et 800 MWc de capacité installée, nous faisons avancer la transition énergétique à pleine vitesse. 
 Ce qui a commencé par des centrales solaires au sol est devenu une entreprise énergétique complète. Aujourd’hui, nous développons et fournissons de l’énergie solaire, du stockage par batteries, du solaire thermique, de l’hydrogène, des réseaux intelligents et bien plus encore. Nous couvrons toute la chaîne de valeur – du développement et de la construction à la gestion de l’énergie et à l’innovation. 
 Depuis 2024 nous étendons nos activités au-delà de notre marché d’origine, avec une présence en Suède, en Allemagne et en France. Notre objectif est ambitieux : développer 7 gigawatts de systèmes énergétiques verts d’ici 2035. Chez Novar, vous rejoindrez une équipe internationale en pleine croissance, animée par la volonté de faire la différence. Nous ne construisons pas seulement des projets énergétiques – nous façonnons les systèmes énergétiques de demain.

 Research Associate - Computer Vision and Deep Learning in the DeCNeC Research Project
 The Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft ( www.fraunhofer.com ) is one of the world's leading organizations for application-oriented research. 74 institutes develop pioneering technologies for our economy and society – more precisely: 30 000 people from technology, science, administration and IT. They know: Anyone who comes to Fraunhofer wants to and can make a difference. For themselves, for us and for the markets of today and tomorrow.
 As part of the DeCNeC research project, we are developing innovative AI-based methods for detecting CSAM (without our researchers working with any actual CSAM imagery).
 Be part of change 
 Research and development in computer vision
 Research, implementation and optimization of methods for the automated detection of pornographic content.
 Image classification and visual representation learning using modern neural network architectures and vision foundation models (e.g. ViT, ConvNeXt, DINOv3, C-RADIO, SigLIP 2).
 Object detection and image segmentation (e.g. YOLO26, RF-DETR, Grounding DINO, SAM 3).
 Semantic image analysis using vision-language models (e.g. Qwen-VL, InternVL).
 Design and execution of scientific experiments
 Collection, cleaning, preparation, annotation and visualization of datasets (e.g. via Embedding Atlas).
 Implementation and analysis of various ML methods (e.g. one-class classification, contrastive learning, fine-tuning, ensemble and fusion methods).
 Hyperparameter optimization, ablation studies and comparative analyses.
 Evaluation of models in terms of detection performance, robustness and generalizability.
 Documentation and publication of scientific results.
 Software development and prototyping
 Development of ML pipelines using established frameworks and libraries (e.g. PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, timm, scikit-learn).
 Development of interactive user interfaces, web applications and research demonstrators (e.g. Gradio, Streamlit, FastHTML, FastAPI, SvelteKit).
 What you contribute 
 Professional requirements
 Completed university degree (Master's or equivalent) in computer science, preferably with a focus on machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL) and computer vision.
 Solid theoretical and practical knowledge of ML and DL.
 Familiarity with modern neural network architectures, especially vision transformers and CNNs.
 Solid knowledge of core ML concepts and methods, in particular classification, fine-tuning, hyperparameter optimization and model evaluation.
 Excellent Python programming skills are essential and will be assessed as part of the selection process!
 Desirable additional qualifications
 Ability and interest in preparing research results and publishing them at international conferences.
 Ability to independently implement and further develop methods from scientific publications.
 Experience with vision foundation models and multimodal AI models.
 Experience with GPU-based training environments, Linux, Git and Docker.
 Knowledge of cybersecurity or digital forensics.
 Personal skills
 Strong analytical and conceptual thinking.
 Independent, structured and scientifically rigorous way of working.
 Willingness to familiarize yourself with new technologies and challenging research questions.
 Team spirit and a responsible approach to sensitive research content.
 What we offer 
 Work at a renowned, internationally leading institute in the field of cybersecurity
 Friendly, open and collegial work environment with a dynamic and creative atmosphere
 Family-friendly work culture with flexible working conditions (various working time models, flexible working hours and locations, flexible work models including the option to occasionally work remotely within the EU in accordance with company regulations, subsidized public transport ticket, support services from pme Familienservice, etc.)
 Company pension plan, capital-forming benefits (vermögenswirksame Leistungen), deferred compensation
 Convenient location (approx. 10 minutes' walk from Darmstadt Central Station), free parking and high-performance charging infrastructure for electric vehicles with preferential rates for employees
 Note: The position is initially limited to two years. We aim for a long-term collaboration.
 The weekly working time is 39 hours. This position is also available on a part-time basis. We value and promote the diversity of our employees' skills and therefore welcome all applications – regardless of age, gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, ideology, disability, sexual orientation and identity. Severely disabled persons are given preference in the event of equal suitability. Our tasks are diverse and adaptable – for applicants with disabilities, we work together to find solutions that best promote their abilities. 
 With its focus on developing key technologies that are vital for the future and enabling the commercial utilization of this work by business and industry, Fraunhofer plays a central role in the innovation process. As a pioneer and catalyst for groundbreaking developments and scientific excellence, Fraunhofer helps shape society now and in the future.  
 Ready for a change? Then apply now and make a difference! Once we have received your online application, you will receive an automatic confirmation of receipt. We will then get back to you as soon as possible and let you know what happens next.

items.jobTitle: Systems Engineer – Utility-Scale Solar Electrical Design
items.jobDescription:
Job Description
 Job Summary
 The Systems Engineer – Utility Scale Solar Electrical Design will be responsible for the electrical design, standardization, and technical evaluation of utility-scale solar PV projects for Enerparc India. The role involves developing optimized solar plant designs, supporting technical due diligence, evaluating key electrical components, and coordinating with cross-functional teams during project development and execution.
 This role is primarily focused on utility-scale solar engineering. As Enerparc continues expanding into hybrid and energy storage projects, selected candidates will also have the opportunity to be trained and upskilled in Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and advanced hybrid plant integration
 Key Responsibilities
 Design & Engineering
 Develop and maintain standardized system designs for PV and BESS including SLDs, layouts, and control philosophies.
 Perform technical assessment and component sizing for PV modules, inverters, batteries, and PCS.
 Support system integration studies, including AC/DC coupling configurations, control logics, and operational modes.
 Prepare and review tendering specifications, employer requirements, and design packages for Solar, BESS components and hybrid systems.
 Conduct energy yield assessments (PVsyst), loss analysis, and design optimization to support commercial and pre-bid teams.
 Review and validate electrical studies including load flow, short-circuit, and protection coordination.
 Coordinate with grid interconnection and protection teams for compliance with CEA, IEC, and IEEE standards.
 Vendor Evaluation & Technical Qualification
 Lead technical evaluation and qualification of solar and BESS component vendors.
 Review test reports, certifications (IEC, UL, IS), and field performance data.
 Participate in factory and site inspections (FAT/SAT) and ensure compliance with design and quality requirements.
 Technical Analysis & Support
 Conduct Solar and BESS techno-economic studies, evaluating performance, sizing, and lifetime degradation.
 Review and benchmark OEM proposals for performance, safety, and reliability.
 Support troubleshooting and post-commissioning technical investigations.
 Collaboration & Continuous Improvement
 Work closely with Pre-Bid, D&E, Quality, and Procurement teams for design alignment and cost optimization.
 Continuously update design standards based on new inverter and BESS technologies.
 Provide training and knowledge sharing within the engineering function on hybrid and storage systems.
 Requirements
 Skills and Qualifications:
 Education: B.E./B.Tech or M.Tech in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or Renewable Energy.
 Experience: 5–8 years in utility-scale solar PV electrical design and engineering, preferably in IPP or EPC environments.
 Technical Competencies:
 Strong understanding of utility-scale solar plant design principles.
 Proficient in PVsyst, AutoCAD, PVCase, ETAP, and MS Office.
 Working knowledge of standards: IEC 62933, IEC 62109, IEEE 1547, IS 16221, CEA Grid Code.
 Soft Skills: Strong analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
 Adaptability: Able to manage multiple projects in a dynamic renewable energy environment.
 Benefits
 What to Expect:
 Work at the forefront of emerging technologies — hybrid solar, energy storage, and hydrogen readiness.
 Opportunity to shape Enerparc’s design standardization and technical frameworks.
 Exposure to cross-country collaboration with global Enerparc teams.
 Occasional travel for vendor evaluations, factory inspections, and project reviews.
 Strong professional and technical growth opportunities within a global renewable energy leader.

items.jobTitle: Ingenieur/in oder Physiker/in (w/m/d) FPGA Design für Distributed Acoustic Sensing Systeme (Hannover)
items.jobDescription:
Das Institut für Satellitengeodäsie und Inertialsensorik (SI) des Deutschen Zentrums für Luft- und Raumfahrt e.V. (DLR) in Hannover, Niedersachsen, widmet sich primär Forschungsfragen im Kontext der Nutzung von Quantentechnologien und Quantensensoren und entwickelt Quantenmesstechniken für innovative Anwendungen, bis hin zur Realisierung von Prototypenlösungen.
 Der Forschungsschwerpunkt der Abteilung „Laserinterferometrische Sensorik“ liegt in der Entwicklung von Laserinterferometern und anderer dazugehöriger optischer Systeme für die hochpräzise Messung von Abstandsänderungen. Typische Anwendungsfelder sind z.B. die Erdbeobachtung, die Navigation, die Inertialsensorik und die Gravitationsphysik. Ein weiterer Forschungsschwerpunkt ist die Erprobung und Entwicklung von Distributed Acoustic Sensing Systemen. 
Die Abteilung entwickelt bereits erfolgreich eingesetzte Konzepte weiter und erforscht neue Sensortopologien und -konzepte und testet diese in Form von Prototypen bis hin zu Flugmodellen im Labor sowie den relevanten Umgebungen.
 Die Abteilung "Laserinterferometrische Sensorik" am Standort Hannover sucht für die Entwicklung von Distributed Acoustic Sensing Systemen eine/n Ingenieur/in oder eine/n Physiker/in (w/m/d) mit abgeschlossenem wissenschaftlichen Hochschulstudium. Konkret wirst du für das Design der benötigten FPGA-Logik und der Software für die Mikrocontroller verantwortlich sein. 
 Deine Aufgaben: 
 Du bist verantwortlich für die Entwicklung und Implementierung der Embedded-Systeme (FPGA und Mikrocontroller), die als Kernelemente der DAS-Interrogatoren dienen – von der Architektur über die Implementierung bis zur Integration in das Gesamtsystem
 Du entwickelst die Ansteuerung und Regelung der optischen Komponenten (z. B. Laser, Modulatoren) über die FPGA- bzw. Mikrocontroller-Plattform
 Du implementierst die Echtzeit-Signalverarbeitung auf der Embedded-Hardware: Digitalisierung, Entmischung, Phasenauflösung und akustische Signalrekonstruktion direkt im Interrogator
 Du entwirfst und validierst die Schnittstellen zwischen Embedded-System und nachgelagerter Host-Verarbeitung (Python/C++) sowie zwischen Interrogator und faseroptischem Messtrakt
 Du konzipierst die Hardware-Architektur der DAS-Ausleseelektronik (Schaltpläne, FPGA-Partitionierung, Takt- und Interfaces) in Abstimmung mit den faseroptischen und mechanischen Anforderungen
 Du baust experimentelle Versuchsstände im Faseroptik-/DAS-Labor auf, bringst die Embedded-Systeme in Betrieb und führst Messungen zur Charakterisierung durch
 Du planst und führst DAS-Feldkampagnen an terrestrischen und marinen Standorten durch und arbeitest interdisziplinär mit Expertenteams aus Mechanik, Faseroptik, Elektronik, Geophysik und Systemtechnik zusammen und wirkst an Design-Reviews, Projektmeetings und der systemweiten Validierung mit
 Das bringst du mit: 
 Abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master/Diplom-Uni) der Ingenieurs- oder Naturwissenschaften (z. B. der Fachrichtung Elektrotechnik und Informationstechnik oder Physik) oder andere für die Tätigkeit relevante Studiengänge
 Erfahrung im Bereich Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS), idealerweise mit nachweisbarer Projektpraxis in der Entwicklung solcher Systeme
 Vertrautheit mit den physikalischen Grundlagen von Φ-OTDR und interferometrischen Messverfahren
 Erfahrung in der Programmierung von FPGAs und von Mikrocontrollern mittels VHDL, respektive C/C++
 Sicherer Umgang mit Simulations- und Programmierumgebungen (MATLAB, Python, C/C++) für die Erstellung von Datenanalyse- und Signalverarbeitungspipelines
 Ausgeprägte Analyse- und Problemlösungskompetenz im Umgang mit komplexen physikalischen Systemen
 Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen!
 Fragen zu dieser Position ( Kennziffer  7023 ) beantwortet dir gerne: 
 Dr. Alexander Koch  
Tel.: +49 421 24420 1091

Hybrid working with two/three days a week in our Edinburgh office, depending on ‘in-office’ support required that week.
 About us
 Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform, on a mission to help more people invest, and invest well.
 We’re building the infrastructure behind the next generation of investing. Our technology already powers some of the UK’s most ambitious fintechs, banks, financial advisers and wealth firms, with close to a million investors relying on Seccl-powered platforms. And we’re now expanding into Europe.
 We’ve got a proven product, strong momentum and big ambitions for what comes next: helping more household-name brands launch and scale investment propositions, entering new markets and replacing outdated investment infrastructure with technology that’s faster, simpler and built for scale.
 We’re proud to be part of Octopus, one of the UK’s most successful privately held investment and technology groups. That gives us the backing and long-term perspective to build something substantial, while keeping the pace and energy of a high-growth business. Seccl and Octopus are both B Corp certified and share a belief that profit and purpose should go hand in hand.
 If you want to help shape the future of investing in the UK and across Europe, you’ll be in good company.
 Check out the Seccl website to see what we’re building and read more about our mission to shape the future of investments.
 The role
 We’re looking for a Junior IT support analyst to join our TechOps team, reporting to the Senior IT support analyst. This role will help us deliver outstanding IT support to Seccl staff as we continue to scale.
 Our TechOps team sits within Engineering and underpins Seccl’s modern workplace. It’s a fast moving, collaborative environment with plenty of variety, from supporting joiners, movers and leavers, to managing the Mac device lifecycle and SaaS admin. You’ll quickly build hands on experience with the latest tech.
 What you’ll own
 Act as the first point of contact for internal IT queries, owning triage and providing first contact resolution where possible
 Meet first response SLAs and keep colleagues updated on ticket progress through clear, friendly communication
 Support the joiner / mover / leaver process, from equipment provisioning and account setup to access changes and deactivation, maintaining an accurate IT asset register
 Keep endpoints compliant with our security standards in a Mac first environment
 Use our ticketing tools (e.g., Jira Service Management) and suggest pragmatic improvements to workflows and automation
 Be a friendly face for TechOps, especially on busy office days - helping new starters settle in and resolving day-to-day issues quickly
 This role’s for you if...
 You’re proficient with Mac and comfortable supporting colleagues in a Mac based environment (essential)
 You have a strong interest in technology, a problem solving mindset and clear, empathetic communication (essential)
 You’re organised, proactive, friendly and confident engaging with people across the business (essential)
 You’re happy to work 2–3 days a week from our Edinburgh office to support colleagues in person (essential)
 You’ve had exposure to Microsoft 365 - Azure AD, Entra, Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive (desirable)
 You’ve used Jamf or other endpoint management (e.g., Intune) and understand the basics (desirable)
 You’ve used Jira Service Management or similar ticketing systems and/or the Atlassian suite (desirable)
 This role isn’t for you if...
 You’re less comfortable in people-facing roles. As the first port of call for IT issues, and one of the first faces employees meet as they join Seccl, strong people skills are essential!
 You’re not comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. Our speed and scalability are what set us apart; you need to be able to act quickly and think on your feet
 You struggle to follow through on ideas. We value people who do what they say they will. If you care about something, you have the freedom here to make it happen
 You don’t like change. You’ll get on great here if you relish the ambiguity of rapid growth and are willing to embrace uncertainty
 What’s in it for you
 We offer a generous mix of benefits designed around the things that matter to our people:
 💰 £27,000 - £30,000 , reviewed annually, plus a 6% employer pension contribution and life assurance
 🌴 27 days’ holiday plus bank holidays , your birthday off and paid dependant leave
 💙 Two volunteering days each year 
 🌎 The option to work abroad for up to six weeks a year 
 🌟 Secclbrate , our recognition programme offering flexible rewards including extra pay, additional holiday and increased learning budget
 🏅 One-month paid sabbatical after eight years 
 🏥 Private medical insurance with AXA Health 
 👪 Enhanced parental leave 
 💻 MacBook and up to £500 towards your home office set-up 
 📖 £750 annual learning budget 
 🌻 Health and wellbeing support , including free therapy through Wellness Cloud and mental health support through Headspace
 🌱 Financial wellbeing benefits , including Octopus Money, the Octopus Share Incentive Plan and will writing through Octopus Legacy
 🎁 Perkbox , with flexible points and a range of discounts and perks
 🚲 Access to Cycle to Work and Octopus Electric Vehicle Leasing 
 Our culture
 We put people first and try hard to create an environment where people feel trusted, heard and able to do their best work.
 We value openness, curiosity and different perspectives. You’ll have the freedom to challenge how things are done, experiment with better ways of working and take real ownership of your impact.
 Check out our Glassdoor page for the latest reviews or our LinkedIn for company updates and insights from the team.
 Interview process
 Interviewing is a two-way process. Our interviews are conversational, with plenty of time for you to get to know us and ask questions too:
 Screening call - 20 mins initial chat with one of our Talent team
 First stage – 45 mins competencies-based interview with the hiring manager and IT support analyst
 Second stage – one hour technical interview or assessment with the hiring manager and the Senior TechOps manager
 We review applications as they come in and may close the role once we have enough candidates to move forward. We’ll keep you updated throughout.
 Everyone’s welcome
 We want to build a diverse and inclusive company full of brilliant people with different skills, experiences and perspectives. All applicants will be considered without regard to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran status, neurodiversity or disability.
 If this sounds like your kind of thing, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to hear from you. 
 Compensation: £27K – £30K

 Job description
 ATMOS Space Cargo is seeking an FPGA Design Engineer (m/f/d) to develop the programmable logic at the heart of the avionics in our PHOENIX return systems. In this role, you will own FPGA designs on AMD devices, from RTL through timing closure and verification. Working closely with avionics, systems engineering, and mission operations, you will follow your designs through qualification, test campaigns, and flight operations. 
 Key responsibilities 
 You will develop, implement, and verify FPGA designs on AMD devices, with a focus on Zynq UltraScale+ and RFSoC, for the avionics of our PHOENIX reentry systems. 
 You will write RTL code in VHDL or Verilog for real-time data processing, sensor interfaces, and communication interfaces in the flight system. 
 You will perform synthesis, place and route, and timing closure, and run functional and formal verification using AMD Vivado and Vitis. 
 You will work with avionics, systems engineering, and mission operations to define interfaces and requirements. 
 You will support qualification and test campaigns, including hardware-in-the-loop and environmental testing, and investigate faults during flight operations. 
 You will contribute to the selection of FPGA devices and development tools for future missions. 
 Profile required
 Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Aerospace Engineering, or a comparable qualification. 
 3+ years of professional experience in FPGA design, ideally with AMD or Xilinx devices such as Zynq UltraScale+, RFSoC, or Kintex and Virtex UltraScale+. 
 Very good knowledge of VHDL or Verilog, together with hands-on experience in AMD Vivado and Vitis. 
 Experience with verification methods such as simulation and test benches, and with timing analysis. 
 A structured, self-directed working style and enjoyment of interdisciplinary teamwork in an international environment. 
 Business-level English; knowledge of German or French is a plus. 
 Preferred qualifications 
 Experience with safety-critical or embedded real-time systems in aerospace, avionics, or automotive. 
 Experience with formal verification alongside simulation-based methods. 
 Experience supporting hardware qualification and environmental test campaigns.

Das Institut für Kommunikation und Navigation des DLR widmet sich der missionsorientierten Forschung in ausgewählten Bereichen der Kommunikation und Navigation.
