 Verantwortung ab dem ersten Tag: Bei uns übernimmst du früh Verantwortung und kannst aktiv an der Weiterentwicklung unserer IT-Landschaft mitwirken.
 Weiterbildung & Entwicklung: Wir unterstützen deine fachliche und persönliche Weiterentwicklung durch Schulungen, Zertifizierungen und individuelle Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten.
 Moderne Technologien & Teamkultur: Arbeite mit Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot und modernen Cloud-Lösungen in einem kollegialen Umfeld mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen.
 Vorsorge & Benefits: Profitiere von einer attraktiven betrieblichen Altersvorsorge über eine Direktversicherung sowie zahlreichen Vergünstigungen und Angeboten über unseren Partner ValueNet.
 Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen und gemeinsam die IT-Landschaft der Prokuras Gruppe weiterzuentwickeln. Bewirb dich jetzt und werde Teil unseres Teams!

Real ownership. Real impact. Build from day one. 
 Are you an ambitious graduate ready to tackle complex , real-world challenges at the intersection of data, strategy and tech? 
 The Future Leaders Graduate Program – Business Analytics at Picnic is a two-year launchpad for exceptional talents. From day one, you join a business team, own a business topic, and become an expert in your field.
 At Picnic, we’re building the future of grocery. Using cutting-edge technology and data-driven innovation, we challenge the status quo and build the world’s smartest, most customer-focused supermarket. 
We move fast, think big, and turn bold ideas into tangible impact.
 Tricks of the trade 
 Lead with ambition : Bring your relentless determination, creativity, and grit. Take the driver’s seat and redefine the grocery shopping experience for millions. You will be expected to think independently, move fast, and deliver results.
 Steep learning curve : Your growth comes from owning real problems, testing your ideas, learning from your mistakes and starting again. You'll blend hands-on training with immediate execution, you’ll move at a pace that accelerates your growth like nowhere else.
 Solve real-life puzzles : Spot opportunities, use tools at the forefront of technology, and own the outcome end to end. Not just making slides, but building the solution yourself.
 Innovate across borders : You’ll collaborate with teams across the Netherlands, Germany, and France, tackling challenges that redefine how Picnic operates at a European scale.
 High-performance environment : You’ll work alongside some of the best teams in analytics and tech, people who set a high bar and expect you to do the same.
 From learning to leading 
 Throughout the two-year program, you’ll own business-critical projects from start to finish, supported by mentorship, learning sessions, and regular feedback.
 You’ll strengthen your leadership skills in project management, storytelling, stakeholder communication, and giving and receiving feedback, while sharpening your technical skills in Python, SQL, Excel, and PowerPoint.
 As your scope grows, so does your responsibility. You might scale your initial project or take on new challenges within the same domain. Either way, the pace is yours to set, and there’s always a new challenge to lead and an opportunity to make an impact. That’s why every journey is unique: there’s no standardized path through the program, just continuous opportunities to learn, and lead.
 Where you’ll make an impact 
 From day one, you’ll be embedded in a business team, taking ownership in one of the following domains:
 Consumer - Drive growth through pricing, supplier strategy, and our market strategy. Think: Shaping our successful market entry into new cities. Your decisions shape how millions of customers experience Picnic.
 Logistics - Build the backbone of Picnic: robotic fulfilment, demand forecasting, route optimization across Europe and much more
 Your superpowers 
 You don't wait for permission. You see a problem, build the solution, and bring people with you, before anyone asks. You've probably already started something: a project, a product, a business, an initiative that didn't exist until you made it happen.
More specifically, you:
 Are about to graduate (or recently graduated) a Masters in a quantitative field 
 Have experience in high-performance environments: consulting, fast-growth startups, or competitive internships.
 Show an entrepreneurial mindset : you build, improve, and take ownership without being asked
 Think like a builder : hands-on, curious, and driven to challenge the status quo with practical solutions
 You have already gained basic knowledge in PowerPoint, Python, SQL, Excel or alternative coding languages 
 EU citizenship or valid EU working permit required .
 Many strong candidates (particularly women) talk themselves out of applying because they don't tick every box. If this excites you and you believe you have what it takes, apply. We only hire when we find the right match. That’s why our selection process is intentionally highly selective. 
   Why Picnic? 
 Grow as we grow . We’re scaling quickly across countries and millions of customers and this is just the start. Grow your impact as we grow; we invest in your path but the driver's seat is always yours.
 Work with other innovators.  Work with a driven, energetic team that builds, wins, and celebrates together (think of legendary Friday drinks, our Ski trip and our parties)
 Kickstart your career.  Earn a competitive salary and step into a program designed to launch your long-term future at Picnic.
 When are you joining?  
 Fall Edition 2026
 Start dates: September, October
 *earlier or later dates can be arranged, please indicate your preference in the application question 
 Spring Edition 2027
 Start dates: February, March
 *earlier or later dates can be arranged, please indicate your preference in the application question 
 📍 Location: Full-time in Paris, with period trips to NL and DE
 There is no deadline : Our aim is to find the most ambitious people out there. We onboard talents on a monthly basis, so whether you join in April or August, you’ll always have a group of people sharing the ride. 
 Picnic Perks 
 🚲Health and Transportation 
Through our partnerships with Malakoff Humanis and OpenUp, you have the opportunity to enroll in our company health insurance plan, as well as free and easy access to professional psychologists, workshops, and practical tools. Additionally, if you commute to work using public transportation, we reimburse 50% of your subscription cost.
 🍉Food 
Since we are located in the center of Paris, there is no on-site cafeteria. However, you will receive meal vouchers worth €11 per day to explore all the delicious restaurants nearby. Our small kitchen is also stocked with tasty snacks and refreshments.
 📈Personal and Professional Development 
You will have the opportunity to develop your skills not only through exciting projects and a dynamic environment but also via training programs offered by Lepaya.
 🏖️All the rest 
You get 25 days of paid vacation, plus additional rest days (RTT) based on the number of days worked in the year. Picnic provides you with a laptop, a phone, and a paid SIM card.
🚀Access to exclusive deals and perks through our Works Council (CSE) and our partner Swile (gift cards, concert tickets, cinema discounts, and more)
 FAQ 
 Do I need a quantitative background? It's a strong advantage, but not a hard requirement. If your internships and projects demonstrate real hands-on ownership and data-driven thinking, we'll consider your application. You do need a Master's degree, basic knowledge of Python or SQL, and relevant work experience.
 Does the program include rotations? No, intentionally. We believe depth creates ownership, and ownership creates impact. Rather than rotating across teams, you’ll go deep in one area, build real expertise, and gradually expand your scope as your impact grows. If you have topic preferences, tell us during the process.
 In what language should I apply? English. Please include your CV and Master's degree transcript or any other relevant test scores (e.g., GMAT)
 What are the long-term opportunities after the program? This program is a fast track into a high-impact career at Picnic, it’s an entry point for a long-term future, not a two-year stopover. 
 Career paths here are as varied as the people on them. Some grow vertically, building deep expertise and a team around them as their project expands. Others move laterally - from Commercial to Fulfilment, Distribution to Customer, or wherever their strengths and ambitions take them. What they share is real ownership, real impact, and a career they shaped themselves.

Job Description:
 About Us
 Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The company is constantly innovating to provide efficient and technologically advanced solutions in aerospace, defense, and connected services. In the commercial aircraft sector, Airbus offers the most modern and fuel-efficient aircraft families. Airbus is also a European leader in defense and security and one of the world's largest space companies. As such, we are actively shaping the technological future to strengthen the security and sovereignty of Europe.
 Role
 As Agentic Engineering Architect, you will design how AI agents do real engineering work at Organization. You’ll join a small, fast-moving team with startup energy, delivering the agentic roadmap for the whole of Engineering. You will work side by side with engineers across our Centres of Competence to find where agents can change how aircraft are designed, simulated and verified. Then you will build those solutions hands-on, from the first demonstrator to TRL 9. This role suits someone who enjoys both the architecture and the build, and who wants their work to shape the next generation of AI-powered vehicle development.
 Location: Munich or Madrid or Toulouse or Paris or Hamburg
 Key Responsibilities
 Shape how agents do engineering work. Design agentic workflows across the engineering lifecycle, from requirements and systems architecture through design, simulation and V&V. Decide how tasks are broken down, which agents do what, how they hold context, and when they hand back to a human. Be equally clear on where agents add real value and where simpler automation is the better answer. 
 Connect agents to the engineering toolchain. Build the integrations that let agents work safely inside PLM, requirements management, SysML v2 / MBSE, CAD and CAE environments. Define clean, auditable tool contracts, so every agent action can be traced back to who asked, what was done and which data was used. 
 Move fast from idea to demonstrator. Work with the Engineering Centres of Competence to find high-impact use cases, then turn them into working demonstrators in weeks, not quarters. Prototype hands-on, test with real engineers, and kill or scale ideas based on evidence, in a team that runs with the pace and ownership of a startup. 
 Build once, reuse everywhere. Turn each solution into modular building blocks (retrieval, requirement parsing, traceability, simulation orchestration) that the next use case can pick up. Keep a growing catalogue of these blocks, so every new demonstrator ships faster than the last. 
 Design for trust and certification from day one. Build human-in-the-loop checkpoints, approval gates and evaluation hooks into every workflow, matched to how critical each task is. Work with assurance and quality specialists so solutions produce the evidence needed to mature towards TRL 9. 
 Take solutions all the way to operations. Agree architecture standards and acceptance criteria with the Digital teams early. That way, solutions matured up to TRL 9 can be handed over for deployment and maintenance without a rebuild. Help shape the platforms behind Organization’s next generation of AI-powered vehicle development.
 Your Profile 
 Required Qualifications
 8-9 years of experience in software engineering or software / systems architecture, including at least 2 years building LLM-based or agentic systems beyond proof of concept. 
 Hands-on experience with multi-agent or tool-using LLM systems: orchestration frameworks, function calling, retrieval and evaluation. 
 Proven experience integrating software with complex engineering or enterprise tools such as PLM, ALM, MBSE or CAE environments. 
 Strong grounding in distributed systems: microservices, APIs, event-driven design and containers. 
 Fluent Python; working knowledge of at least one more language such as Java, Go or C++. 
 Comfortable working directly with engineers to turn loosely defined problems into working solutions. 
 Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience in aerospace, defence, automotive or another safety-critical, regulated industry. 
 Familiarity with systems engineering practice (ARP4754B, ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288) and SysML v2. 
 Experience with knowledge graphs, ontologies or semantic technologies. 
 Track record of taking a solution from prototype to operational use. 
 Experience working in a startup or innovation team.

About Tritium Fuel Cycle (TFC) GFG is designing a first-of-a-kind (FOAK) fusion power plant (FPP) to deliver 1 GW of electrical power in the 2040s. The “GIGA” plant will be based on a stellarator magnetic confinement fusion device, operating continuously on a deuterium-tritium (D-T) fuel cycle.  Prior to this, the smaller “Gauss Industrial Demonstrator (GID-170)” will be deployed in the mid-2030s.
 While deuterium can be extracted from seawater, tritium is a tightly controlled radioactive isotope with an extremely limited global supply. Therefore, both GID-170 and GIGA must utilise closed tritium fuel cycle infrastructure, to ensure that unburnt tritium is fully recycled back to the stellarator and not released to the environment. Meanwhile, the tritium consumed by the fusion reaction must be replenished using tritium breeding blankets (TBB).
A first-of-a-kind dedicated tritium fuel cycle (TFC) facility, suitable for continuously supporting a stellarator device, must be designed, built and commissioned. It will adopt a multi-loop process architecture, each loop comprising many deeply integrated subsystems. Developing such a facility presents unique engineering challenges: the supply chain is still emerging, commercial process simulation tools lack dedicated TFC libraries, suitable off-the-shelf equipment is not always available, and some technologies have relatively low technology readiness levels (TRLs). 
A conceptual design is currently under development, with the project then progressing into pre-front-end engineering design (pre-FEED) in 2028, followed by front-end engineering design (FEED) and design for manufacturing phases. Completion of the overall design phase (for GID-170) must be achieved by 2032. 
 About the role GFG is looking for several Tritium Process Engineers to join the TFC department and develop the GID-170 and GIGA TFC facilities. The roles will contribute to the continued development and optimisation of the overall fuel cycle architecture and its subsystems. Activities will include managing design requirements; developing process flow diagrams (PFDs), piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), heat and mass balances (HMBs) and the Basis of Design (BoD); selecting technologies; sizing and arranging equipment; and contributing to safety-related design. The roles may also involve supporting equipment prototype development and testing with technology developers and research partners.
We welcome candidates with complementary strengths in process design and process modelling and simulation, with systems engineering experience also desirable. These specialisations sit within the same engineering function, and candidates are not expected to have equal expertise across all areas. The number of appointments and balance of responsibilities will reflect the successful candidates’ experience and technical strengths. Drawing on their specialist expertise, successful candidates will work collaboratively on design development, modelling, analysis and optimisation to assess design alternatives and inform robust, well-documented design decisions.
The TFC comprises a wide range of technologies and subsystems, requiring the department to manage multiple sub-projects and work packages in parallel. Each engineer will contribute across several activities and will be expected to take ownership of specific tasks or subsystems, or lead work packages, depending on their experience. The roles will involve close collaboration with engineers from the same and other disciplines at national and international partner organisations, research institutions and suppliers, as well as with colleagues across disciplines and departments within GFG. Given the specific challenges associated with tritium, close collaboration with Nuclear Safety and Export Control specialists will also be essential.
During conceptual design, successful candidates will work closely with the Head of Tritium Fuel Cycle to address the strong interdependencies between subsystems and develop a coherent, integrated design. As the project moves into pre-FEED, they will be expected to take greater day-to-day ownership of their assigned areas and drive design development through pre-FEED and FEED, while maintaining close coordination across subsystem interfaces. As the project progresses, the roles will evolve to support design for manufacture, procurement and commissioning of the GID-170 TFC systems, followed by further development and refinement of the TFC design for GIGA.
 Main responsibilities Process definition and systems engineering Identify, define and manage system requirements and interfaces across TFC subsystems and the overall plant architecture. 
 Develop and optimise the fuel cycle architecture, assessing alternative subsystem technologies, their respective advantages and disadvantages, technology readiness levels (TRLs), and potential system configurations. 
 Develop process flow diagrams (PFDs) for individual TFC subsystem blocks and the overall plant architecture. 
 Participate in the development of piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), identification and sizing of key components, and equipment layout. 
 Develop and maintain representative heat and mass balances to support process definition, system integration and design decisions. 
 Process modelling and simulation Develop, apply and improve process simulation models for individual TFC subsystem blocks and the overall plant architecture, using tools such as Aspen Plus, Aspen Custom Modeler, Python and dedicated proprietary software, as appropriate. 
 Support the development and integration of custom models and, where appropriate, contribute to the development of dedicated simulation tools. 
 Use modelling and simulation to assess system performance, compare technology options and operating configurations, support component sizing, and inform process optimisation and design decisions. 
 Documentation of assumptions, uncertainty and applicability limits, and perform model validation when suitable data becomes available. 
 Work collaboratively with internal and external modelling specialists to ensure consistency between simulation results, engineering requirements and the evolving plant design. 
 Cost, safety and risk management Identify and manage design risks, developing effective risk-reduction strategies and action plans. 
 Identify applicable standards, regulations and codes, and ensure that these are considered throughout the design process.  
 Participate in hazard, safety and accident analyses, including hazard identification (HAZID) and hazard and operability (HAZOP) studies, and contribute to the definition of safety functions and development of the safety case. 
 Contribute to capital and operational expenditure (CAPEX/OPEX) estimates. 
 Design development and delivery Develop design documentation and specifications, including contributions to the Basis of Design and design philosophies. 
 Document design studies, verification and assessment activities, engineering assumptions and design decisions. 
 Support the design development, procurement and testing of prototypes for key components, in collaboration with technology developers, suppliers and research partners. 
 Provide engineering support for R&D activities conducted in-house and with external partners and collaborators. 
 Project coordination and collaboration Lead specific technical tasks or work packages assigned by the Head of TFC, in line with experience and expertise. 
 Take ownership of specific subsystems throughout the pre-FEED and FEED studies, as assigned by the Head of TFC, in line with experience and expertise. 
 Participate in technical meetings with partners, suppliers, research institutions and other collaborators. 
 Collaborate closely with other engineering disciplines and contribute to the integration of TFC systems within the wider fusion plant. 
 As required, undertake other relevant duties in support of project objectives. 
 GID-170 delivery (in the 2030s) Support the procurement and installation activities of the GID-170 TFC facilities. 
 Develop commissioning plans and operating instructions. 
 The balance between process design, systems engineering, and process modelling and simulation will depend on each candidate’s background and area of expertise. All engineers are expected to work collaboratively across these areas, ensuring that modelling activities inform engineering decisions and that process design is supported by robust analysis. 
 Qualification and educational requirements Required  qualifications: 
 Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in chemical engineering, process engineering, nuclear engineering, or a closely related discipline*.   
 *In the case of a closely related discipline, the degree should be supported by relevant chemical engineering experience. 
 A minimum of 3 years design experience working as a Process Engineer in an industrial environment. 
 Additional desirable qualifications relevant to process modelling and simulation : 
 A PhD or EngD in Chemical or Process Engineering or a closely related field. 
 Competences and preferred skills 1. Common skills 
 Essential 
 All applicants should demonstrate: 
 In-depth knowledge of chemical engineering principles, including thermodynamics, heat and mass transfer, process dynamics, and relevant transport phenomena. 
 Experience in the development of industrial-scale process engineering installations in complex environments requiring regulatory approval (ideally nuclear projects or similar). 
 Experience in the development of processes involving different fluids and conditions (cryogenic, vacuum, atmospheric pressure gas, high-pressure gas (up to 100 bara), liquid, etc.). 
 Experience in the design and development of integrated treatment unit operations (purification, separation, conditioning, etc.), ideally in the gas phase, and in the hydrogen or nuclear sectors. 
 Proficiency in at least one established process simulation tool, such as Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, UniSim, gPROMS, ProMax, CHEMCAD or equivalent. 
 Experience in requirements capture, documentation and management. 
 Experience working alongside multiple other engineering disciplines, such as mechanical, electrical, control, thermal and nuclear engineers. 
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams of engineers, technologists and physicists. 
 A proactive and self-motivated approach, with strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills. 
 Professional working proficiency in English.  
 Desirable 
 All applicants would benefit from demonstrating: 
 Knowledge of tritium fuel cycle technologies and/or hydrogen isotope separation. Hands-on experience working with tritium would be an advantage. 
 Experience with the design or analysis of pumping technologies, heat exchangers or other key process equipment. 
 Familiarity with magnetic fusion systems and/or nuclear power plant systems. 
 Familiarity with environmental, nuclear safety and other relevant regulatory requirements.  
 Knowledge of systems engineering and an understanding of configuration management and risk management. 
 Understanding of equipment qualification, manufacture, testing, inspection and pragmatic usability. 
 Knowledge of German or other European languages. 
 2. Specialist Skills 
 Candidates are expected to demonstrate strengths in one or more of the following areas, depending on their background and specialisation. 
 Process design and systems engineering 
 Experience in developing process architectures, heat and mass balances, PFDs and P&IDs, and in supporting equipment selection, sizing and integration. 
 Experience in developing Basis of Design (BoD) documentation, design philosophies, specifications, design descriptions and justifications. 
 Ability to assess alternative process technologies and configurations, considering performance, safety, technical maturity and operational requirements. 
 Experience in translating system requirements and process analysis into engineering specifications and design decisions. 
 Familiarity with process safety codes, standards and regulations, as well as safety-by-design principles, including the ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) approach. 
 Experience in engaging with potential technology suppliers and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). 
 Process modelling and simulation 
 Proficiency in process modelling tools such as Aspen Custom Modeler, gPROMS custom modelling or equivalent. 
 Proficiency in at least one programming or scientific computing language, such as Python, Julia, MATLAB, Octave or C++. 
 Strong understanding of numerical methods applied to chemical engineering, including ordinary and partial differential equations (ODEs and PDEs), differential-algebraic equations (DAEs), discretisation techniques and numerical convergence. 
 Knowledge of numerical optimisation methods and their implementation, with the ability to apply them to process analysis and design optimisation. 
 Experience developing custom process models, integrating subsystem models or analysing dynamic process behaviour, along with model automation and analysis, to assess system performance, compare design options and support process optimisation is an advantage. 
 We are recruiting engineers with complementary technical strengths. Applicants who meet the common essential criteria and have relevant capability in one specialist profile are encouraged to apply; experience in every technology or software package listed is not expected. 
 The balance of responsibilities and the level of technical ownership will be agreed according to each successful candidate’s experience and the needs of the programme, with opportunities for candidates to grow and develop into greater technical ownership.

About EASE
 EASE builds active, AI-powered exoskeletons for logistics and manufacturing. As a TUM spin-off, we have just started series production, and paid pilots with well-known logistics companies have led to first purchase orders.  The role
 Our exoskeletons are deployed in real warehouses and production plants and capture what video-only datasets miss: body pose, joint kinematics, interaction torques, vision, and hand forces from real human work. Your job is to turn that data into skills our humanoid can actually perform, so that human workers and robots can work side by side on the same tasks.
 What you'll do
 Map human motion onto humanoid kinematics and close the embodiment gap
 Train manipulation and whole-body policies with imitation and reinforcement learning
 Evaluate in Isaac Lab or MuJoCo and on our in-house humanoid, and measure the value of our data
 Define what data training needs and help build our training setup, including GPU compute
 Turn new research on robot foundation models and VLAs into prototypes

 Master's or PhD in robotics, CS, ML or similar, with hands-on experience from industry or research
 Imitation or reinforcement learning on real robots (e.g. Diffusion Policy, ACT, PPO)
 Strong Python and PyTorch; C++ is a plus
 Physics simulation and sim-to-real transfer
 Solid kinematics, dynamics and control
 Nice to have
 Learning from human data (egocentric video, motion capture, retargeting)
 Humanoids, legged robots or exoskeletons; publications at CoRL, RSS, ICRA or NeurIPS
 Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. What you have built matters more than a perfect match.

 Data almost nobody else has, from a product in series deployment
 Our own humanoid and the chance to build Physical AI at EASE from the ground up
 Competitive salary plus virtual stock options (VSOP)
 Flexible hours, hybrid in Munich, mobility benefit

**Das ist zukünftig dein Job**

* Unterstützung bei der Einhaltung regulatorischer Anforderungen und sicherheitsrelevanter Standards im Luftfahrtumfeld
**Das erwartet dich bei uns**
* Betriebliche Altersvorsorge
* Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag
* Satte Rabatte mit Einkaufsvergünstigungen, z. B. bei Reisen, Elektronik oder Autos
* Bei uns kannst du eigene Ideen einbringen und aktiv mitgestalten

* Networking und einfach Spaß haben bei Teamevents, Weihnachtsfeiern oder Sommerfesten

* Spannende und abwechslungsreiche Projekte bei innovativen Unternehmen
**Das bringst du mit**
* Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium der Informatik, Elektrotechnik, Nachrichtentechnik, Sicherheitstechnik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung
* Erfahrung in der Entwicklung, Integration oder Betreuung kryptografischer Systeme
* Gute Kenntnisse gängiger Kryptografieverfahren wie RSA, AES, PKI oder vergleichbarer Technologien
* Verständnis sicherer Kommunikationsprotokolle und sicherheitskritischer Systemarchitekturen
* Erfahrung in der Systemintegration, Anforderungsanalyse und technischen Dokumentation
* Kenntnisse luftfahrtrelevanter Standards oder IT-Sicherheitsnormen von Vorteil
* Sicherer Umgang mit Engineering-Tools wie MATLAB, IBM DOORS oder Enterprise Architect
* Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse zwingend sowie gute Englischkenntnisse erforderlich
Lust auf die nächste Herausforderung? Dann sollten wir uns unbedingt kennenlernen! Am schnellsten geht es, wenn du dich direkt bewirbst. Lass uns gemeinsam das nächste Level nehmen und Technologie nach vorn bringen!

Would you like to develop the embedded software behind Ambu’s next generation of medical technology? Do you have experience with Embedded Linux and enjoy solving technical challenges? Are you motivated by working closely with colleagues across software, electronics and test?
Then this might be your defining moment. Join us as Embedded Software Developer in our global Embedded Software team in Augsburg, Germany or Ballerup, Denmark!
 Together, We Shape What's Next
 At Ambu, your expertise can make a difference to the people delivering and receiving care. Across our portfolio, our products support more than 100 million patients worldwide every year.
As part of Global R&D, you’ll join skilled colleagues who share their knowledge, take ownership and work through challenges together. You’ll contribute to a strong innovation pipeline spanning devices and digital solutions, with EndoIntelligence™ bringing hardware, software and AI together to support the full endoscopy workflow.
 About The Role
 As an Embedded Software Developer, you’ll contribute to developing and evolving our modular embedded software platform, connecting hardware with application software. You’ll work hands-on with Embedded Linux, Yocto, C and C++, developing reliable solutions for our future products.
Working closely with software, electronics, test and application teams, you’ll be involved in development, debugging, testing and ongoing improvements to the platform. You’ll contribute your experience to technical discussions while learning from colleagues with different areas of expertise.
As our Embedded Software team expands across Ballerup and Augsburg, you’ll have opportunities to develop your skills and take on increasing technical responsibility. We offer a hybrid working model, with at least three days per week in the office to support regular on-site collaboration.
 Key Responsibilities
 Your main responsibilities will include:
 Develop and maintain our custom Linux distribution, board support packages (BSPs), firmware and drivers.
 Design, implement, debug and test embedded software solutions.
 Collaborate with hardware, application software and test engineers across locations.
 Contribute to technical discussions, code reviews and knowledge sharing within the team.
 Improve our development practices, tooling and software quality.
 Support technical documentation required for medical-device development and cybersecurity compliance.
 Suggested candidate profile
 Skills
 Skills and experience can be earned in many ways, and we understand that the best fit for the role cannot be fully described on paper. You are, however, likely to succeed in this position if you have:
 A degree in electronics engineering, computer science or a related field.
 Around five or more years of professional experience in embedded software development.
 Solid hands-on experience with Embedded Linux.
 Experience with Yocto or similar embedded Linux build systems.
 Programming experience in C and/or C++.
 Experience developing, debugging and testing embedded software.
 Strong communication skills in spoken and written English.
 Experience in any of the following areas would also be valuable:
 Board bring-up, BSP development or maintenance, Device Tree and Linux driver development.
 Embedded security technologies and concepts, such as Secure Boot and Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs).
 Software development in safety-critical or regulated industries, such as medical devices or automotive.
 Microcontrollers, preferably ARM-based, and real-time operating systems such as Zephyr.
 Python or shell scripting.
 Automated testing, including hardware-in-the-loop, unit testing and Pytest.
 CI/CD and modern embedded software development practices.
 AI agents or AI-assisted development tools within software development workflows.
 You enjoy solving technical problems and working closely with others. You share your knowledge, remain curious about different approaches and are motivated to keep developing your expertise. You’re comfortable contributing your ideas and taking ownership of your work as part of a team.
 About The Team
 You’ll join our growing Embedded Software team, currently consisting of 10 colleagues across Ballerup, Denmark, and Augsburg, Germany. The team brings together developers and test engineers with different technical backgrounds, working together to develop our modular embedded platform.
You’ll report to the Head of Embedded Software, who is based in Ballerup, Denmark, and collaborate closely with colleagues at our headquarters and in Augsburg. Our way of working is open, collaborative and agile. We value knowledge sharing and technical curiosity, with colleagues supporting one another as we develop the platform and our skills. The role involves travel between the sites for up to approximately 20 days per year.
 Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter
 You’ll have the opportunity to deepen your expertise in embedded software and see your work become part of products used in clinical practice. Working across disciplines, you’ll contribute your ideas and learn from colleagues with different technical perspectives.
We offer a wide range of professional, social and financial employee benefits, alongside exciting technical challenges and opportunities for continuous professional and personal development.
 How To Apply
 We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please submit your application in English.

Job Description:
 About Us
 Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The company is constantly innovating to provide efficient and technologically advanced solutions in aerospace, defense, and connected services. In the commercial aircraft sector, Airbus offers the most modern and fuel-efficient aircraft families. Airbus is also a European leader in defense and security and one of the world's largest space companies. As such, we are actively shaping the technological future to strengthen the security and sovereignty of Europe.
 Role
 As AI Foundations Engineer, you will help build and run the platform that every AI agent, within Airbus Engineering, depends on. You'll join a small, fast-moving team with startup energy, delivering the agentic roadmap for the whole of Engineering. You will work hands-on across model hosting, retrieval pipelines, security and monitoring, turning architecture decisions into systems that run reliably every day. This role suits an engineer early in their career who wants to grow fast on hard infrastructure problems and help shape the next generation of AI-powered vehicle development.
 Location: Munich or Madrid or Toulouse or Paris or Hamburg
 Key Responsibilities
 Deploy and run AI models. Set up, test and maintain model hosting across managed APIs and self-hosted open-weights models (vLLM or equivalent). Help measure latency, throughput and GPU use, and make sure each workload runs on the right setup for its data classification. 
 Build retrieval pipelines. Develop and maintain the pipelines that make engineering documents usable by agents: ingestion, chunking, embeddings and vector databases. Test retrieval quality and improve it step by step with the wider team. 
 Implement security guardrails. Put the agreed security controls in place: access management, secrets handling, sandboxed execution, prompt-injection defences and masking of sensitive and export-controlled data. Work with IT security on reviews and fixes. 
 Set up monitoring and evaluation. Instrument agents and models with tracing, logging and dashboards for latency, errors, cost and quality. Support continuous evaluation runs and flag issues early. 
 Keep the team moving fast. Build and maintain the environments, CI/CD pipelines and shared services that let a new demonstrator go from idea to running in days. Try out new models and tools and report on what works. 
 Support handover to operations. Help prepare documentation, runbooks and readiness checks, so solutions matured up to TRL 9 transfer cleanly to the Digital teams for deployment and maintenance.
 Your Profile
 Required Qualifications
 3-5 years of experience in software, cloud, DevOps or MLOps engineering, including hands-on work with LLM or ML systems. 
 Practical experience deploying or serving models, through APIs or self-hosted. 
 Working knowledge of retrieval systems, embeddings and vector databases. 
 Experience with containers, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code and CI/CD. 
 Good grasp of security basics: access control, secrets management, network segmentation. 
 Strong Python and scripting skills. 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience with GPU infrastructure or on-premise environments. 
 Familiarity with observability tools (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana) and LLM tracing or evaluation tools. 
 Exposure to regulated industries or export-control constraints. 
 Cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP) or Kubernetes certifications. 
 Experience in a startup or innovation team.
 What We Offer
 The unique opportunity to shape the future of aircraft engineering at a world-leading aerospace company. 
 An inspiring work environment that combines the innovative power of a startup with the expertise of an established technology site. 
 A team of brilliant minds working together on a grand vision for Europe's technological sovereignty. 
 Excellent professional development opportunities within the Airbus group. 
 Interested? Apply now!

Job Title: Service Engineer – Port Machinery or Cranes 
 Location: Bedburg, Germany
 The role is primarily based at the Bedburg yard for PDI and workshop activities, with occasional field assignments at customer sites.
 About SANY Europe: 
 SANY Europe is a subsidiary of SANY Group, a global leader in the manufacturing of construction and port machinery. With a strong commitment to innovation, reliability, and customer satisfaction, SANY Europe provides high-performance equipment and exceptional after-sales support across the European market.
 Position Overview: 
 We are looking for a motivated and skilled Service Engineer to join our after-sales service team. The successful candidate will be responsible for technical support, maintenance, commissioning, and troubleshooting of SANY heavy equipment products. Candidates with experience in either port machinery or crane equipment are encouraged to apply.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Perform commissioning, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair work on SANY heavy equipment, including port machinery and crane products.
 Diagnose and resolve mechanical, hydraulic, electrical, and control system faults in a timely and professional manner.
 Provide technical support to customers, dealers, and internal teams through on-site visits, remote assistance, phone, and email.
 Conduct inspections, fault analysis, and root cause investigations to improve equipment reliability and uptime.
 Prepare service reports, maintenance records, technical documentation, and warranty-related reports.
 Support equipment installation, testing, commissioning, and handover activities at customer sites.
 Deliver technical training to customers, operators, dealers, and service partners on equipment operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
 Collaborate with engineering, product support, and quality teams to provide field feedback and support continuous product improvement.
 Ensure all service activities comply with company safety standards, local regulations, and customer requirements.
 Travel within Germany and occasionally across Europe to support customers and service operations.
 Requirements: 
 Technical degree or equivalent qualification in mechanical, electrical, or mechatronic engineering.
 Minimum 3 years of experience servicing heavy equipment.
 Experience in either of the following fields:
 Port Machinery (Reach Stackers, Material Handlers, Telescopic Handlers, etc.)
 Crane Equipment (Mobile Cranes, Truck Cranes, All Terrain Cranes, Crawler Cranes, etc.)
 Strong knowledge of hydraulics, electrical systems, and diesel engines.
 Ability to read and interpret technical drawings and schematics.
 Fluent in English; German is an advantage.
 Willingness to travel within Germany and Europe.
 Valid driver's license.
 We Offer: 
 Competitive compensation and benefits package.
 Dynamic and international working environment.
 Opportunities for professional growth and development.
 Work with cutting-edge machinery and technologies in the port equipment industry.
 Equal Opportunity Employer: 
 Sany EU is committed to equal employment opportunity and welcomes applications from all qualified individuals regardless of gender, age, origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or other legally protected characteristics.
 Data Protection Notice: 
 Personal data submitted as part of the application process will be processed exclusively for recruitment and related employment purposes in accordance with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable German data protection law. Your application data will be treated confidentially and retained only for as long as necessary for these purposes or as required or permitted by law.

Willkommen im Institut für Solarforschung. Wir beschäftigen uns damit, die Einführung erneuerbarer Energien voranzutreiben, in dem wir zusammen mit industriellen Partnern Solarsysteme zur Wärme-, Strom und Brennstofferzeugung entwickeln.
 Die Forschenden der Gruppe Materialien entwickeln und erproben innovative Materialien und Beschichtungen für verschiedene Energieanwendungen. Zur Verfügung stehen u. a. eine Magnetron-Sputteranlage, ein industrielles Glasreinigungssystem, sowie eine Laminiereinheit zum Verbinden beschichteter Substrate. Zudem verfügt das Institut über ein umfassend ausgestattetes Charakterisierungslabor mit Rasterelektronenmikroskop (SEM) inkl. fokussiertem Ionenstrahl (FIB), verschiedenen Spektrometern (UV/VIS/NIR, FTIR) und Klimakammern zur Qualifizierung der Haltbarkeit der erzeugten Materialien.
 Das erwartet dich 
 Du brennst für erneuerbare Energien? Dann schließe dich unserem Institut in Almería (Spanien) an – einem der sonnenreichsten Orte Europas – und entwickle innovative Werkstoffe für die Energiewende. Damit leistest du einen wichtigen Beitrag zum Übergang zu einer CO₂-neutralen Gesellschaft. Dein Forschungsfeld umfasst u. a.:
 Materialien und Beschichtungen zur passiven Strahlungskühlung
 Photoaktive Schichten für thermochemische Hochtemperaturverfahren
 Hochtemperaturmaterialien und-schichten für konzentrierende Solarthermie
 Neuartige hybride Materialien und Beschichtungen für die simultane photovoltaische und thermische Energiewandlung
 Materialien und Beschichtungen zur solaren Wasseraufbereitung
 Du arbeitest in einem internationalen Umfeld – auf der Plataforma Solar de Almería in enger Zusammenarbeit mit unserem spanischen Partner CIEMAT.
 Deine Aufgaben 
 Entwicklung und Erprobung neuer Materialbeschichtungen für Solarenergie, nachhaltige Brennstoff-Synthese und thermochemische Technologien, sowie passive Strahlungskühlungsschichten
 Nutzung der verfügbaren Ressourcen und der Team-Expertise sowie Inbetriebnahme neuer Geräte und Aufbau vertiefter Anwendungs-Expertise
 Entwicklung neuer Projektideen und deren Umsetzung; Aufbau neuer Kooperationen mit Industrie und Forschung
 Veröffentlichung der Ergebnisse in wissenschaftlichen Zeitschriften und Präsentation auf internationalen Konferenzen
 Das bringst du mit 
 Master-Abschluss und Berufserfahrung oder Promotion in Materialwissenschaft, Chemie, Physik, Ingenieurwissenschaften oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet
 Erfahrung in Material- und Beschichtungstechnik (idealerweise Sputtertechnologie) und/oder Materialcharakterisierung
 Sehr gute Fähigkeiten in Problemlösung, Recherche und Kommunikation
 Verantwortungsvolles Arbeiten und Teamfähigkeit in einem internationalen Umfeld
 Erfahrung in der Verfassung wissenschaftlicher Fachartikel und Projektberichte
 Erfahrung oder ausgeprägtes Interesse an Projektmanagement und der Antragstellung für internationale Forschungsprojekte
 Sichere Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift; Spanischkenntnisse von Vorteil
 Die Vergütung erfolgt je nach Qualifikation und Aufgabenübertragung bis Entgeltgruppe 14 TVöD.

 Das DLR steht für Vielfalt, Wertschätzung und Gleichstellung aller Menschen. Wir fördern eigenverantwortliches Arbeiten und die individuelle Weiterentwicklung unserer Mitarbeitenden im persönlichen und beruflichen Umfeld. Dafür stehen dir unsere zahlreichen Fort- und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten zur Verfügung. At our company, it's all about #OneTeam! Join gridscale and help shape the future of the cloud together with OVH.
 As a leading tech company, we've been working for over two decades to reduce our environmental footprint - with innovative solutions and an open cloud designed to be sustainable from the ground up: #SustainableByDesign.
 Within our #OneTeam, you'll shape the automation-first framework that lets every product team ship securely and at speed on top of OPCP, our On-Prem Cloud Platform.
 Our Tech Stack 🚀 
 · Kubernetes · GitOps · FluxCD / ArgoCD · Ansible · Terraform · OpenStack · Linux · CI/CD
 · Python · Bash · Go · Observability (Metrics, Logs, Traces) · LLMs · Agentic Coding Tooling
 Your Role💻 
 As a Site Reliability Engineer, you'll work at the intersection of platform engineering, AI-driven tooling and security by design. Together with your team, you'll build the framework to package and deploy software solutions on top of OPCP - turning vague product ideas into repeatable, observable and self-healing services. You'll work on the conception, automation and operation of the platform, drive continuous improvements and help new teams onboard with the framework and OPCP. Working hand in hand with developers, security specialists and AI researchers, you keep an overview in ambiguous situations, analyze systems and make well-founded decisions based on that analysis.
 AI-assisted engineering is part of our daily toolchain because it materially improves how we build and operate the platform – from spec-driven development with LLM assistance and knowledge-base-driven retrieval for incident response and design to agentic coding workflows and faster runbook authoring and review. We are investing in this direction as a structural part of our engineering practice and are looking for teammates who already work this way – not because it is trendy, but because they have seen it compound their own output.

 Design, build and maintain the Cloud Store packaging framework that standardizes how software is delivered on OPCP.

 Create and curate agentic coding environments : custom agents and sub-agents, slash commands, hooks and prompt engineering pipelines that become everyday developer tools.

 Write, publish and continuously improve OPCP onboarding runbooks and best-practice guides for internal product teams.

 Develop, version and operate the Infrastructure as Code stack (Terraform, Ansible) that underpins the platform, and take part in our on-call rotation .

Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain? 
 The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain that moves them from donation to resale is offline, manual and broken.
 Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We run a B2B marketplace where resellers and stores buy clothing in bulk, and we build the AI systems that digitise the supply chain behind it.
 Our buyers sell on eBay, Vinted, Depop, Whatnot, eBay Live and TikTok Shop, or run vintage stores from Brick Lane to Paris to New York. They source graded stock from wholesalers and rag houses across many countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion that can grade, price and categorise an item from a single photo.
 We are now going well beyond vintage. Live sellers can sell almost anything, and there is an opportunity for Fleek to be the backend for B2B resale. We've now started onboarding customers alongside supply from Japan, South Korea, the Philippines and Thailand.
 Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill and tripled in size year on year. We've raised ~$50M from a16z, Y Combinator, HV Capital and others, and recently closed our Series B. Our advisors and private investors include operators behind Depop, Shopify and Postmates.
 We're looking for people who want to build something that matters, and move fast doing it.
 About the role 
 You'll join the GTM team as our GTM Engineer, reporting to our GTM lead and working day to day with the new business team. You'll own the system we use to find and win customers, on both sides of the marketplace.
 On the demand side, that means online resellers, live sellers and physical stores in the UK, Europe and the US, buying vintage, deadstock, new with tags and luxury. On the supply side, it means the brands, brokers, wholesalers and rag houses who sell to them. As we add new categories and markets, the system has to find those customers too.
 We already have pipelines that scrape marketplaces and load leads into our CRM. The next step is everything after that: putting the right leads first, reaching them well, and learning from every outcome. You'll own the engine end to end, from the first scrape to the revenue each new customer brings in.
 This is not a typical B2B SaaS GTM engineering role. You won't spend your days wiring a CRM to a LinkedIn sequencer or building dashboards. Everyone on our commercial team builds their own tools with AI. You'll take on the problems they can't: systems that improve themselves, infrastructure that scales, and outreach that works within limits set by platforms like Meta.
 The role is part engineer, part product manager and part commercial. You won't carry a closes target, but you'll own every metric that moves it.
 The problem you'll solve 
 We want a system that finds the right customers, puts them in order, reaches out, and gets better every week. It runs as a loop:
 Find. Source leads across marketplaces and social platforms, for every segment and market we sell into.
 Prioritise. Score each lead on the signals that predict a good customer, not just a likely reply.
 Reach out. Contact them on Instagram, WhatsApp, email, phone or LinkedIn, personalised by AI and handed to a rep at the right moment.
 Learn. Feed every outcome back into scoring. If a store replied but wasn't a fit, similar leads drop down the list, so we stop spending tokens and rep time on them. Then back to step 1.
 To make that loop work, you'll build a second brain for GTM: one layer that holds everything we know about a customer, with models and agents running on top. That includes the messages we sent and how they replied, how fast they replied and closed, what they sell and where, what they click and search for in our app, what they told our reps on calls, and how much they spend and how well they retain.
 The same data powers our account management team, who look after customers once they've placed their first orders. Matching each buyer with the right supply is one of their next big problems, and you'll help solve it.
 What you'll do 
 Own the acquisition engine. Learn how our current pipelines work and improve them. If a rebuild is the right call, make the case for it, and keep leads flowing to the reps while you build.
 Source at scale in new segments. Find vintage stores, live sellers, deadstock and luxury buyers, and new suppliers, in every market we enter.
 Build the scoring and feedback loop. Define what a good lead looks like for each segment, then keep refining it on what actually closes and what actually spends.
 Engineer multi-channel outreach. Instagram, WhatsApp, email, calls and LinkedIn, personalised by AI and built around real limits like Instagram DM caps and Meta restrictions.
 Own the funnel numbers. Leads sourced per day on each platform, reply rate, conversion rate and GMV per close by source. Use them to decide what to fix next.
 Sit with the reps and talk to customers. Learn why a lead is good and how each segment wants to be sold to. Then automate the repetitive parts of the rep's day.
 Turn repeat work into agents. Qualification, first messages, reply handling, dedupe and CRM hygiene should run without a person.
 Keep it efficient. Every system you build should make sense on cost per lead and unit economics.
 Connect acquisition to retention. Make sure new customers land cleanly with account management, and help build the buyer-to-supply matching they rely on.
 What you bring 
 A strong technical background. You've built and run real systems, such as data pipelines, scrapers, models or production infrastructure. You've done more than configure tools.
 An AI-first mindset, a step ahead. You build with Claude and other models every day and know where agents work and where they break. Our commercial team is very AI-literate, and you'll push them further.
 Curiosity about the customer. You want to know why one lead closes and another doesn't, and how each segment wants to be sold to. You're happy on a call with a reseller.
 Problem solving over playbooks. You take an ambiguous problem, form your own view and ship something that works. We'd rather hire someone who works it out than someone repeating what worked elsewhere.
 Ownership. You challenge how things are done, bring your own recommendations and explain why.
 Rigour with numbers. You track honest metrics, know where your funnel leaks and judge your systems on results.
 Excitement about the space. You see how big the opportunity is and want to build it.
 Nice to have 
 GTM, growth or RevOps experience, including outbound you've run yourself
 Founder or early-startup experience where you owned growth end to end
 Experience building ranking, scoring or recommendation models
 Experience building for marketplaces, resellers, live selling or independent retail
 Familiarity with secondhand, vintage, deadstock or luxury fashion
 Running multi-channel outbound under platform limits (DM caps, deliverability, warm-up)
 What good looks like 
 First 30 days: you know the current pipelines inside out, have sat with the reps and have shipped your first improvements, with leads still flowing. You've shared your plan to improve what's there or rebuild it, and why.
 3 months: one data layer joins outreach, replies, closes, app activity, call notes and spend. Scoring runs on it, and the loop from outcome back to scoring is live for at least one segment.
 6 months: the system improves itself. Each week it sources more leads, and better ones, across our segments and markets, and conversion and GMV per close are rising.
 12 months: the engine is the backbone of acquisition across vintage, deadstock and luxury, on both demand and supply. Agents run the repeat work, and you focus on what to build next.
 What you'll get 
 Competitive salary plus a performance bonus tied to qualified pipeline
 Generous equity: being on Fleek means you'll own a part of it
 Comprehensive healthcare coverage
 A collaborative team in a lovely office in the heart of East London
 Access to founders. We're a small team and they're heavily involved (and good fun!)
 Exclusive employee discounts to buy on Fleek
 Access to borrow any item from our collection of vintage and reworks in the office
 A disproportionate level of responsibility and the chance to drive massive impact
 How we work 
 High ownership, non-hierarchical and fast-moving. We hire problem solvers, not order takers. If you have a better way to do something, and it moves the numbers at a sensible cost, go for it.
 Our commercial team builds its own tools, so each new hire starts more effective than the last. People who deliver get more scope quickly. You'll work embedded with the GTM team, ship fast and see your work in the pipeline within days, not quarters.
 The practicalities 
 Location: London HQ, E1, Spitalfields / Shoreditch
 Work model: in person, with trust-based flexibility
 Stage: post-Series B, hyper-growth
 Team: a GTM team of 5 AEs in new business and 3 AMs in account management, within 100+ people across London, India and Pakistan
 Process: an intro call, then an in-person case study in two parts: one on the business with our GTM lead, one technical with our engineers
 Our values 
 Five values shape how we work at Fleek:
 Dream Big and Disrupt Yourself: Push the most ambitious version of what you're building. Step out of your comfort zone. Nothing is out of reach.
 Absolute Ownership: The buck stops with you. Drive initiatives to completion. Experiment, learn, persevere. The job isn't done until the job is done.
 Curiosity Leads the Way: Don't accept anything at face value. Ask questions you don't know the answer to. That's how you innovate.
 Talk to the Customer: Deeply understand their challenges, motivations and ambitions. Every decision starts with the customer at the centre.
 Embrace Diversity: A global team building for a global supply chain. Bring your authentic self and embrace the diversity of everyone you encounter.
 Ready to build the infrastructure for the world's fastest-growing fashion economy? If you want to work on genuinely hard problems, with a world-class team, at a company that's tripling annually, we'd love to hear from you.

- Bearbeitung und Durchführung von Harness-AIT-Aufgaben in anspruchsvollen Raumfahrtprojekten
- Vorbereitung, Durchführung und Dokumentation von Harness-Integrations- und Testaktivitäten
- Abarbeitung von Harness-AIT-Anforderungsdokumentationen, Integrations- und Testplänen, Integrationsvorschriften sowie Reports
- Selbstständige Durchführung von Testplänen und Messungen mit mechanischen und elektrischen Mess- und Prüfgeräten
- Integration und Check-out von Test-Harnesses in Satellitenbaugruppen und -strukturen gemäß kundenspezifischen Anforderungen
- Durchführung und Unterstützung bei der mechanischen Satellitenintegration
- Mitarbeit bei Testkampagnen im In- und Ausland
- Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Standorten sowie europäischen Unterauftragnehmern
- Sicherstellung einer fachgerechten, qualitätsorientierten und termingerechten Durchführung der AIT-Aktivitäten
Fachliche Anforderungen
- Abgeschlossene technische Ausbildung, idealerweise als Elektroniker oder Fluggerätelektroniker (m/w/d), mit Weiterbildung zum staatlich geprüften Techniker Elektrotechnik (m/w/d) oder vergleichbarer Qualifikation
- Alternativ: Abgeschlossenes Studium als Ingenieur (m/w/d) im Bereich Elektrotechnik, Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik, Mechatronik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung, idealerweise mit vorheriger praktischer Ausbildung im elektrotechnischen Bereich
- praktische Erfahrung in der Harness-Fertigung, einschließlich der eingesetzten Verarbeitungswerkzeuge und der Fertigungskontrolle
- Erfahrung im Umgang mit Crimp-, Löt- und Verbindungstechniken sowie ein ausgeprägtes Verständnis für deren qualitätsgerechte Verarbeitung
- Erfahrung im Bereich der mechanischen und elektrischen Messtechnik
- Technisches Verständnis für Mechanismen und Systemelemente von Satelliten und Raumfahrzeugen
- Erfahrung in der mechanischen Integration von Satelliten sowie idealerweise Kenntnisse der gängigen Standardprozeduren und Qualitätsanforderungen der Luft- und Raumfahrtindustrie
- Sicherer Umgang mit technischen Dokumentationen, Integrationsvorschriften, Prüfplänen und Testprozeduren
- Eine ESA-Zertifizierung für Crimpen nach ECSS-Q-ST-70-26 ist von Vorteil
- Eine ESA-Zertifizierung für Löten nach ECSS-Q-ST-70-08 ist von Vorteil
- Selbstständige, strukturierte und sorgfältige Arbeitsweise sowie ein hohes Qualitätsbewusstsein
- Teamfähigkeit und Freude an der Zusammenarbeit in internationalen Projektteams

**Folgende Aufgaben erwarten Sie:**
- Umfassende Einarbeitung in die bestehende Linux-Systemkonfiguration sowie die zugehörigen Konfigurationsoberflächen und intensive Einbindung in die Systeme
- Einarbeitung in die bestehende Middleware-Lösung sowie Unterstützung bei der Umsetzung neuer Anforderungen im Rahmen der Softwarepflege und Softwareänderung
- Mitwirkung bei der Härtung von Systemen zur Erfüllung von IT-Sicherheitsanforderungen sowie kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung bestehender Sicherheitsmaßnahmen

- Ausgeprägte Teamfähigkeiten sowie ein hohes Maß an Selbstständigkeit, Belastbarkeit und Zuverlässigkeit
- Bereitschaft zu gelegentlichen Dienstreisen innerhalb Deutschlands

Unser zusätzliches Angebot – was wir Ihnen bieten und was Sie von uns erwarten können

###### Beschreibung
Für unseren Kunden aus der Windenergie suchen wir einen Project Engineer Rotorblade \(m/w/d\) in Vollzeit. In dieser Position übernehmen Sie die Leitung strategisch wichtiger Rotorblattprojekte und verantworten deren erfolgreiche Umsetzung hinsichtlich Qualität, Kosten und Terminen. Dabei arbeiten Sie mit interdisziplinären und internationalen Teams zusammen und steuern anspruchsvolle Projekte von der Planung bis zur Umsetzung. Die Position ist auf zwei Jahre befristet.
###### IHRE AUFGABEN
- Sie leiten strategisch wichtige Rotorblattprojekte und tragen dabei die Verantwortung für Qualität, Kosten und Termine.
- Die Projektplanung sowie die Steuerung technologischer und personeller Ressourcen gehören ebenfalls zu Ihrem Verantwortungsbereich.
- Darüber hinaus führen Sie Projekt-Audits und Gate-Reviews durch und stellen eine strukturierte Bewertung des Projektfortschritts sicher.
- Sie übernehmen das qualifizierte Reporting gegenüber relevanten Stakeholdern sowie dem Bereichsmanagement.
- Zur optimalen Projektsteuerung setzen Sie Best-Practice-Ansätze ein und unterstützen damit eine nachhaltige Umsetzung der Projekte.
- Zudem führen und koordinieren Sie interdisziplinäre und internationale Projektteams.
- Sie identifizieren Verbesserungspotenziale und relevante Markttrends und stellen gleichzeitig die Einhaltung von Qualitäts- und Informationssicherheitsstandards sicher.
###### ÜBER UNSEREN KUNDEN
Unser Auftraggeber ist Teil eines weltweit führenden Unternehmens im Bereich erneuerbare Energien und zählt zu den größten Herstellern von Windenergieanlagen. Am Standort Aurich werden innovative Lösungen für Windkrafttechnik entwickelt und umgesetzt, die zu den modernsten der Branche zählen. Das Unternehmen steht für höchste Qualitätsstandards, Nachhaltigkeit und technische Exzellenz. Sie arbeiten in einem internationalen Umfeld, das von zukunftsorientierten Projekten, technischer Kompetenz und einer offenen, wertschätzenden Unternehmenskultur geprägt ist. Persönliche Weiterentwicklung und eigenverantwortliches Arbeiten werden gezielt gefördert.
###### IHR PROFIL
- Sie verfügen über einen Hochschulabschluss in Windenergietechnik, Maschinenbau, Mechatronik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung.
- Zudem bringen Sie mindestens sieben Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung in mittelgroßen bis großen Projekten mit.
- Eine nachweisbare Projektmanagement-Erfahrung sowie eine entsprechende Zertifizierung setzen wir voraus.
- Darüber hinaus verfügen Sie über Erfahrung mit Engineering- und Fertigungsprozessen in der Windenergie, idealerweise mit Schwerpunkt Rotorblatt.
- Ausgeprägte Kommunikations-, Führungs- und Mentoringfähigkeiten in einem internationalen Umfeld zeichnen Sie ebenfalls aus.
- Strategisches Denken und eine ausgeprägte Problemlösungskompetenz verbinden Sie mit Belastbarkeit und Flexibilität.
###### IHRE BENEFITS
- Attraktives Monatsgehalt
- Planbare Arbeitszeiten in Tagschicht
- Betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit Arbeitgeberzuschuss
- E-Bike-Leasing
- Persönliche Betreuung durch erfahrene Ansprechpartner
- Verantwortungsvolle Position in einem internationalen Umfeld
- Mitarbeit an strategisch wichtigen Projekten im Bereich Windenergie

📌 About Us 
 Posha is building robot kitchens for the future.
 Our first product, the Posha Countertop was recognized as one of TIME’s Best Inventions of 2025 and received rave reviews from The Verge and WIRED for bringing robotics and AI into everyday kitchens.
 We’re a fast-growing Series A–funded startup backed by Accel Partners and we’re just getting started.
 See it in action: https://youtu.be/Ubd6NkZOEkM?si=SFex-isehKHzvZs_ 
 🤔 What can I expect from this role? 
 Posha is one of the rare robotics startups building production-grade consumer robots , with hundreds of units deployed in real homes .
 You own the electrical design of robotics cooking system that packs power electronics(induction heating), analogs (sensors, actuators) and high-speed design (cameras, display and a GPU) into one consumer robotic system.
 🔧 What will my work responsibilities look like if I join Posha? 
 Design the induction heating power stage, from mains input to inverter and coil, and keep its noise away from the sensitive electronics next to it.
 Design the analog and digital circuits that read the product's sensors and drive its motors and actuators.
 Own the high-speed design for the camera, display and GPU, getting signal and power integrity right next to a switching power stage.
 Review every schematic before it goes to layout, whether it was drawn in-house or by a vendor.
 Take boards from bring-up through safety and EMC certification into production with our contract manufacturers.
 😍 What makes you a match for us? 
 You have a B.E./B.Tech in Electrical or Electronics Engineering and 5+ years designing board-level electronics for a product that shipped.
 You decided what the circuit should be and owned the schematic yourself; drawing the layout from someone else's design doesn't count.
 You have hands-on power electronics experience (inverters, motor drives or switching supplies) along with analog, digital or high-speed design.
 You debug boards yourself in the lab and have released hardware to production.
 🚀 What The World Thinks of Posha 
 Posha is comparable to Tesla FSD 
 “ Posha is a fairly good sign that the future is closer than I thought ” - The Verge 
 Posha’s tagline is “See dinner cook itself, and it largely lives up to this.” - WIRED 
 Why Posha? 
 Few organizations offer challenges similar to ours. Building completely autonomous cooking robots requires thinking from first principles and building from ground up.
 We believe that Posha is a generational company with the opportunity to alter the trajectory of how food is cooked inside homes today. This opportunity is parallel to how autonomous cars have made an impact.
 This role will be at the forefront of this opportunity.

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.
 What is the role
 Platform Infrastructure provides the infrastructure, tooling, processes and services that more than a thousand Elastic engineers depend on. We are about 110 people across ten teams in three groups: Core Infrastructure, Reliability Engineering, and Engineering Productivity & Developer Experience. We run the multi-cloud platform underneath Elastic Cloud Hosted and Serverless, the shared Kubernetes platform other Elastic teams build on, the observability estate that shows Cloud engineers what production is doing, and the release path the whole Elastic Stack ships through.
 As an SRE here you take an engineering approach to reliability. You write the Go, Python and Terraform that replaces manual work, you carry the on-call rotation for what your team runs, and you work with Cloud engineering to close the gaps you find.
 Elastic is expanding its Serverless offerring, and most of what we build sits underneath it. Current work includes packing hundreds of customer projects onto shared clusters, PrivateLink and static IPs, new regions, a single identity layer across the stack, and new government regions. We are also replacing manually managed services with code-managed systems, which lets the platform grow without the on-call load growing with it.
 Why join us
 The scale is large. We run across multiple cloud providers and many regions, and some teams operate 200+ production deployments of our own product.
 We are customer zero for Elastic Cloud Hosted, Serverless and the observability and security products, so new features land on our systems first and our feedback goes back to the product teams.
 The engineers who use what you build are a thousand colleagues you can go and talk to.
 On-call follows the sun, which keeps the burden outside working hours small.
 We are fully distributed across EMEA, NASA and APJ and the work happens in writing, so you control how you run your day.
 What You Will Be Doing
 You own systems end to end as the DRI on a project, and you break the work down yourself.
 Own the outcome of projects on your team’s roadmap as the DRI, breaking the work down and pulling in help when you need it.
 Operate and harden the infrastructure that other Elastic engineers depend on, managed as code with Terraform, Go and Python.
 Build tools and services that remove manual work.
 Carry the on-call rotation for what your team runs, drive incidents to resolution and write RCAs that lead to lasting fixes.
 Improve observability, runbooks and documentation so the on-call load gets lighter over time.
 Review code and designs, and act as a second set of eyes on production changes to critical infrastructure.
 Raise risks and ideas without being asked, and mentor engineers with less experience.
 Give feedback to the Elastic product teams on the features that reach our systems first.
 What You Bring
 3+ years in SRE, platform engineering or infrastructure engineering, including real time operating what you built.
 Experience with Terraform at multi-workspace scale.
 Strong software engineering fundamentals in Go or Python, the languages most of what we build is written in.
 Extensive experience carrying on-call, resolving incidents under pressure and writing RCAs that hold up under review.
 How you work
 You take an ambiguous project, come back with a plan and own it to the end.
 You say when an estimate or a sequence is wrong before the team commits to it.
 You write clearly, because we work across nine time zones and the work happens in tickets and channels.
 You stay calm when something is broken, communicate while you work and write the follow-up that stops it happening again.
 Additional Information - We Take Care of Our People 
 As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. Whether you’re looking to launch a new career or grow an existing one, Elastic is the type of company where you can balance great work with great life. Your age is only a number. It doesn’t matter if you’re just out of college or your children are; we need you for what you can do.
 We strive to have parity of benefits across regions and while regulations differ from place to place, we believe taking care of our people is the right thing to do.
 Competitive pay based on the work you do here and not your previous salary
 Health coverage for you and your family in many locations
 Ability to craft your calendar with flexible locations and schedules for many roles
 Generous number of vacation days each year
 Increase your impact - We match up to $2000 (or local currency equivalent) for financial donations and service
 Up to 40 hours each year to use toward volunteer projects you love
 Embracing parenthood with minimum of 16 weeks of parental leave
